### <a id="forms"></a>4&#46;10 Forms[](#forms)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Element&#35;Forms](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element#Forms)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome61&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera52&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;16&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android5&#43;Safari iOS3&#46;2&#43;Chrome Android61&#43;WebView Android61&#43;Samsung Internet8&#46;0&#43;Opera Android47&#43;

#### <a id="introduction&#45;4"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1 Introduction[](#introduction-4)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

A form is a component of a web page that has form controls&#44; such as text&#44; buttons&#44; checkboxes&#44; range&#44; or color picker controls&#46; A user can interact with such a form&#44; providing data that can then be sent to the server for further processing &#40;e&#46;g&#46; returning the results of a search or calculation&#41;&#46; No client&#45;side scripting is needed in many cases&#44; though an API is available so that scripts can augment the user experience or use forms for purposes other than submitting data to a server&#46;

Writing a form consists of several steps&#44; which can be performed in any order&#58; writing the user interface&#44; implementing the server&#45;side processing&#44; and configuring the user interface to communicate with the server&#46;

##### <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;1 Writing a form&#39;s user interface[](#writing-a-form's-user-interface)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

For the purposes of this brief introduction&#44; we will create a pizza ordering form&#46;

Any form starts with a <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#44; inside which are placed the controls&#46; Most controls are represented by the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; which by default provides a text control&#46; To label a control&#44; the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element"></a><code>[label](#the-label-element)</code> element is used&#59; the label text and the control itself go inside the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[label](#the-label-element)</code> element&#46; Each part of a form is considered a <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;paragraph"></a>[paragraph](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#paragraph)&#44; and is typically separated from other parts using <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;p&#45;element"></a><code>[p](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-p-element)</code> elements&#46; Putting this together&#44; here is how one might ask for the customer&#39;s name&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
</form>
```

To let the user select the size of the pizza&#44; we can use a set of radio buttons&#46; Radio buttons also use the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; this time with a <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute with the value <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;radio&#45;button&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;radio&#41;"></a><code>[radio](#radio-button-state-(type=radio))</code>&#46; To make the radio buttons work as a group&#44; they are given a common name using the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-name)</code> attribute&#46; To group a batch of controls together&#44; such as&#44; in this case&#44; the radio buttons&#44; one can use the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#46; The title of such a group of controls is given by the first element in the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>&#44; which has to be a <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element&#46;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
</form>
```

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Changes from the previous step are highlighted&#46;

To pick toppings&#44; we can use checkboxes&#46; These use the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element with a <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;2"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute with the value <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;checkbox&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;checkbox&#41;"></a><code>[checkbox](#checkbox-state-(type=checkbox))</code>&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
</form>
```

The pizzeria for which this form is being written is always making mistakes&#44; so it needs a way to contact the customer&#46; For this purpose&#44; we can use form controls specifically for telephone numbers &#40;<a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements with their <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;3"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute set to <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;telephone&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;tel&#41;"></a><code>[tel](#telephone-state-(type=tel))</code>&#41; and email addresses &#40;<a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements with their <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;4"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute set to <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;email&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;email&#41;"></a><code>[email](#email-state-(type=email))</code>&#41;&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
</form>
```

We can use an <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element with its <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;5"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute set to <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;time&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;time&#41;"></a><code>[time](#time-state-(type=time))</code> to ask for a delivery time&#46; Many of these form controls have attributes to control exactly what values can be specified&#59; in this case&#44; three attributes of particular interest are <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code>&#44; <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;max"></a><code>[max](#attr-input-max)</code>&#44; and <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;step"></a><code>[step](#attr-input-step)</code>&#46; These set the minimum time&#44; the maximum time&#44; and the interval between allowed values &#40;in seconds&#41;&#46; This pizzeria only delivers between 11am and 9pm&#44; and doesn&#39;t promise anything better than 15 minute increments&#44; which we can mark up as follows&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900"></label></p>
</form>
```

The <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> element can be used to provide a multiline text control&#46; In this instance&#44; we are going to use it to provide a space for the customer to give delivery instructions&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900"></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea></textarea></label></p>
</form>
```

Finally&#44; to make the form submittable we use the <a id="writing&#45;a&#45;form&#39;s&#45;user&#45;interface&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code> element&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900"></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

##### <a id="implementing&#45;the&#45;server&#45;side&#45;processing&#45;for&#45;a&#45;form"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;2 Implementing the server&#45;side processing for a form[](#implementing-the-server-side-processing-for-a-form)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

The exact details for writing a server&#45;side processor are out of scope for this specification&#46; For the purposes of this introduction&#44; we will assume that the script at <code>https&#58;&#47;&#47;pizza&#46;example&#46;com&#47;order&#46;cgi</code> is configured to accept submissions using the <a id="implementing&#45;the&#45;server&#45;side&#45;processing&#45;for&#45;a&#45;form&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;enctype&#45;urlencoded"></a><code>[application&#47;x&#45;www&#45;form&#45;urlencoded](#attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded)</code> format&#44; expecting the following parameters sent in an HTTP POST body&#58;

<strong><code>custname</code></strong>

Customer&#39;s name

<strong><code>custtel</code></strong>

Customer&#39;s telephone number

<strong><code>custemail</code></strong>

Customer&#39;s email address

<strong><code>size</code></strong>

The pizza size&#44; either <code>small</code>&#44; <code>medium</code>&#44; or <code>large</code>

<strong><code>topping</code></strong>

A topping&#44; specified once for each selected topping&#44; with the allowed values being <code>bacon</code>&#44; <code>cheese</code>&#44; <code>onion</code>&#44; and <code>mushroom</code>

<strong><code>delivery</code></strong>

The requested delivery time

<strong><code>comments</code></strong>

The delivery instructions

##### <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;3 Configuring a form to communicate with a server[](#configuring-a-form-to-communicate-with-a-server)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

Form submissions are exposed to servers in a variety of ways&#44; most commonly as HTTP GET or POST requests&#46; To specify the exact method used&#44; the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;method"></a><code>[method](#attr-fs-method)</code> attribute is specified on the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#46; This doesn&#39;t specify how the form data is encoded&#44; though&#59; to specify that&#44; you use the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;enctype"></a><code>[enctype](#attr-fs-enctype)</code> attribute&#46; You also have to specify the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;url"></a>[URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the service that will handle the submitted data&#44; using the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;action"></a><code>[action](#attr-fs-action)</code> attribute&#46;

For each form control you want submitted&#44; you then have to give a name that will be used to refer to the data in the submission&#46; We already specified the name for the group of radio buttons&#59; the same attribute &#40;<a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-name)</code>&#41; also specifies the submission name&#46; Radio buttons can be distinguished from each other in the submission by giving them different values&#44; using the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;value"></a><code>[value](#attr-input-value)</code> attribute&#46;

Multiple controls can have the same name&#59; for example&#44; here we give all the checkboxes the same name&#44; and the server distinguishes which checkbox was checked by seeing which values are submitted with that name — like the radio buttons&#44; they are also given unique values with the <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;value&#45;2"></a><code>[value](#attr-input-value)</code> attribute&#46;

Given the settings in the previous section&#44; this all becomes&#58;

``` text
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname"></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel"></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email name="custemail"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery"></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

There is no particular significance to the way some of the attributes have their values quoted and others don&#39;t&#46; The HTML syntax allows a variety of equally valid ways to specify attributes&#44; as discussed <a id="configuring&#45;a&#45;form&#45;to&#45;communicate&#45;with&#45;a&#45;server&#58;syntax&#45;attributes"></a>[in the syntax section](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#syntax-attributes)&#46;

For example&#44; if the customer entered &#34;Denise Lawrence&#34; as their name&#44; &#34;555&#45;321&#45;8642&#34; as their telephone number&#44; did not specify an email address&#44; asked for a medium&#45;sized pizza&#44; selected the Extra Cheese and Mushroom toppings&#44; entered a delivery time of 7pm&#44; and left the delivery instructions text control blank&#44; the user agent would submit the following to the online web service&#58;

``` text
custname=Denise+Lawrence&custtel=555-321-8642&custemail=&size=medium&topping=cheese&topping=mushroom&delivery=19%3A00&comments=
```

##### <a id="client&#45;side&#45;form&#45;validation"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;4 Client&#45;side form validation[](#client-side-form-validation)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Form&#95;validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Forms/Form_validation)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari5&#43;Chrome4&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera≤12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS4&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android≤37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android≤12&#46;1&#43;

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

Forms can be annotated in such a way that the user agent will check the user&#39;s input before the form is submitted&#46; The server still has to verify the input is valid &#40;since hostile users can easily bypass the form validation&#41;&#44; but it allows the user to avoid the wait incurred by having the server be the sole checker of the user&#39;s input&#46;

The simplest annotation is the <a id="client&#45;side&#45;form&#45;validation&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;required"></a><code>[required](#attr-input-required)</code> attribute&#44; which can be specified on <a id="client&#45;side&#45;form&#45;validation&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements to indicate that the form is not to be submitted until a value is given&#46; By adding this attribute to the customer name&#44; pizza size&#44; and delivery time fields&#44; we allow the user agent to notify the user when the user submits the form without filling in those fields&#58;

``` text
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel"></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email name="custemail"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

It is also possible to limit the length of the input&#44; using the <a id="client&#45;side&#45;form&#45;validation&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;maxlength"></a><code>[maxlength](#attr-fe-maxlength)</code> attribute&#46; By adding this to the <a id="client&#45;side&#45;form&#45;validation&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> element&#44; we can limit users to 1000 characters&#44; preventing them from writing huge essays to the busy delivery drivers instead of staying focused and to the point&#58;

``` text
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel"></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email name="custemail"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments" maxlength=1000></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

When a form is submitted&#44; <a id="client&#45;side&#45;form&#45;validation&#58;event&#45;invalid"></a><code>[invalid](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-invalid)</code> events are fired at each form control that is invalid&#46; This can be useful for displaying a summary of the problems with the form&#44; since typically the browser itself will only report one problem at a time&#46;

##### <a id="enabling&#45;client&#45;side&#45;automatic&#45;filling&#45;of&#45;form&#45;controls"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;5 Enabling client&#45;side automatic filling of form controls[](#enabling-client-side-automatic-filling-of-form-controls)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

Some browsers attempt to aid the user by automatically filling form controls rather than having the user reenter their information each time&#46; For example&#44; a field asking for the user&#39;s telephone number can be automatically filled with the user&#39;s phone number&#46;

To help the user agent with this&#44; the <a id="enabling&#45;client&#45;side&#45;automatic&#45;filling&#45;of&#45;form&#45;controls&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> attribute can be used to describe the field&#39;s purpose&#46; In the case of this form&#44; we have three fields that can be usefully annotated in this way&#58; the information about who the pizza is to be delivered to&#46; Adding this information looks like this&#58;

``` text
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname" required autocomplete="shipping name"></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel" autocomplete="shipping tel"></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email name="custemail" autocomplete="shipping email"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments" maxlength=1000></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

##### <a id="improving&#45;the&#45;user&#45;experience&#45;on&#45;mobile&#45;devices"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;6 Improving the user experience on mobile devices[](#improving-the-user-experience-on-mobile-devices)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

Some devices&#44; in particular those with virtual keyboards can provide the user with multiple input modalities&#46; For example&#44; when typing in a credit card number the user may wish to only see keys for digits 0&#45;9&#44; while when typing in their name they may wish to see a form field that by default capitalizes each word&#46;

Using the <a id="improving&#45;the&#45;user&#45;experience&#45;on&#45;mobile&#45;devices&#58;attr&#45;inputmode"></a><code>[inputmode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-inputmode)</code> attribute we can select appropriate input modalities&#58;

``` text
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname" required autocomplete="shipping name"></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel" autocomplete="shipping tel"></label></p>
 <p><label>Buzzer code: <input name="custbuzz" inputmode="numeric"></label></p>
 <p><label>Email address: <input type=email name="custemail" autocomplete="shipping email"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments" maxlength=1000></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

##### <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;7 The difference between the field type&#44; the autofill field name&#44; and the input modality[](#the-difference-between-the-field-type,-the-autofill-field-name,-and-the-input-modality)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

The <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;inputmode"></a><code>[inputmode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-inputmode)</code> attributes can seem confusingly similar&#46; For instance&#44; in all three cases&#44; the string &#34;<code>email</code>&#34; is a valid value&#46; This section attempts to illustrate the difference between the three attributes and provides advice suggesting how to use them&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;2"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute on <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements decides what kind of control the user agent will use to expose the field&#46; Choosing between different values of this attribute is the same choice as choosing whether to use an <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; a <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> element&#44; a <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#44; etc&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;2"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> attribute&#44; in contrast&#44; describes what the value that the user will enter actually represents&#46; Choosing between different values of this attribute is the same choice as choosing what the label for the element will be&#46;

First&#44; consider telephone numbers&#46; If a page is asking for a telephone number from the user&#44; the right form control to use is <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;telephone&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;tel&#41;"></a><code>[&#60;input type&#61;tel&#62;](#telephone-state-(type=tel))</code>&#46; However&#44; which <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;3"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> value to use depends on which phone number the page is asking for&#44; whether they expect a telephone number in the international format or just the local format&#44; and so forth&#46;

For example&#44; a page that forms part of a checkout process on an e&#45;commerce site for a customer buying a gift to be shipped to a friend might need both the buyer&#39;s telephone number &#40;in case of payment issues&#41; and the friend&#39;s telephone number &#40;in case of delivery issues&#41;&#46; If the site expects international phone numbers &#40;with the country code prefix&#41;&#44; this could thus look like this&#58;

``` text
<p><label>Your phone number: <input type=tel name=custtel autocomplete="billing tel"></label>
<p><label>Recipient's phone number: <input type=tel name=shiptel autocomplete="shipping tel"></label>
<p>Please enter complete phone numbers including the country code prefix, as in "+1 555 123 4567".
```

But if the site only supports British customers and recipients&#44; it might instead look like this &#40;notice the use of <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;tel&#45;national"></a><code>[tel&#45;national](#attr-fe-autocomplete-tel-national)</code> rather than <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;tel"></a><code>[tel](#attr-fe-autocomplete-tel)</code>&#41;&#58;

``` text
<p><label>Your phone number: <input type=tel name=custtel autocomplete="billing tel-national"></label>
<p><label>Recipient's phone number: <input type=tel name=shiptel autocomplete="shipping tel-national"></label>
<p>Please enter complete UK phone numbers, as in "(01632) 960 123".
```

Now&#44; consider a person&#39;s preferred languages&#46; The right <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;4"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> value is <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;language"></a><code>[language](#attr-fe-autocomplete-language)</code>&#46; However&#44; there could be a number of different form controls used for the purpose&#58; a text control &#40;<a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;text&#45;&#40;type&#61;text&#41;&#45;state&#45;and&#45;search&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;search&#41;"></a><code>[&#60;input type&#61;text&#62;](#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search))</code>&#41;&#44; a drop&#45;down list &#40;<a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[&#60;select&#62;](#the-select-element)</code>&#41;&#44; radio buttons &#40;<a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;radio&#45;button&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;radio&#41;"></a><code>[&#60;input type&#61;radio&#62;](#radio-button-state-(type=radio))</code>&#41;&#44; etc&#46; It only depends on what kind of interface is desired&#46;

Finally&#44; consider names&#46; If a page just wants one name from the user&#44; then the relevant control is <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;text&#45;&#40;type&#61;text&#41;&#45;state&#45;and&#45;search&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;search&#41;&#45;2"></a><code>[&#60;input type&#61;text&#62;](#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search))</code>&#46; If the page is asking for the user&#39;s full name&#44; then the relevant <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;5"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> value is <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;name"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-autocomplete-name)</code>&#46;

``` text
<p><label>Japanese name: <input name="j" type="text" autocomplete="section-jp name"></label>
<label>Romanized name: <input name="e" type="text" autocomplete="section-en name"></label>
```

In this example&#44; the &#34;<a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;section"></a><code>[section&#45;&#42;](#attr-fe-autocomplete-section)</code>&#34; keywords in the <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;6"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> attributes&#39; values tell the user agent that the two fields expect <em>different</em> names&#46; Without them&#44; the user agent could automatically fill the second field with the value given in the first field when the user gave a value to the first field&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The &#34;<code>&#45;jp</code>&#34; and &#34;<code>&#45;en</code>&#34; parts of the keywords are opaque to the user agent&#59; the user agent cannot guess&#44; from those&#44; that the two names are expected to be in Japanese and English respectively&#46;

Separate from the choices regarding <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;3"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> and <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;7"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code>&#44; the <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;attr&#45;inputmode&#45;2"></a><code>[inputmode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-inputmode)</code> attribute decides what kind of input modality &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; virtual keyboard&#41; to use&#44; when the control is a text control&#46;

Consider credit card numbers&#46; The appropriate input type is <em>not</em> <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;number&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;number&#41;"></a><code>[&#60;input type&#61;number&#62;](#number-state-(type=number))</code>&#44; [as explained below](#when-number-is-not-appropriate)&#59; it is instead <a id="the&#45;difference&#45;between&#45;the&#45;field&#45;type&#44;&#45;the&#45;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#44;&#45;and&#45;the&#45;input&#45;modality&#58;text&#45;&#40;type&#61;text&#41;&#45;state&#45;and&#45;search&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;search&#41;&#45;3"></a><code>[&#60;input type&#61;text&#62;](#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search))</code>&#46; To encourage the user agent to use a numeric input modality anyway &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; a virtual keyboard displaying only digits&#41;&#44; the page would use

``` text
<p><label>Credit card number:
                <input name="cc" type="text" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]{8,19}" autocomplete="cc-number">
</label></p>
```

##### <a id="input&#45;author&#45;notes"></a>4&#46;10&#46;1&#46;8 Date&#44; time&#44; and number formats[](#input-author-notes)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

In this pizza delivery example&#44; the times are specified in the format &#34;HH&#58;MM&#34;&#58; two digits for the hour&#44; in 24&#45;hour format&#44; and two digits for the time&#46; &#40;Seconds could also be specified&#44; though they are not necessary in this example&#46;&#41;

In some locales&#44; however&#44; times are often expressed differently when presented to users&#46; For example&#44; in the United States&#44; it is still common to use the 12&#45;hour clock with an am&#47;pm indicator&#44; as in &#34;2pm&#34;&#46; In France&#44; it is common to separate the hours from the minutes using an &#34;h&#34; character&#44; as in &#34;14h00&#34;&#46;

Similar issues exist with dates&#44; with the added complication that even the order of the components is not always consistent — for example&#44; in Cyprus the first of February 2003 would typically be written &#34;1&#47;2&#47;03&#34;&#44; while that same date in Japan would typically be written as &#34;2003年02月01日&#34; — and even with numbers&#44; where locales differ&#44; for example&#44; in what punctuation is used as the decimal separator and the thousands separator&#46;

It is therefore important to distinguish the time&#44; date&#44; and number formats used in HTML and in form submissions&#44; which are always the formats defined in this specification &#40;and based on the well&#45;established ISO 8601 standard for computer&#45;readable date and time formats&#41;&#44; from the time&#44; date&#44; and number formats presented to the user by the browser and accepted as input from the user by the browser&#46;

The format used &#34;on the wire&#34;&#44; i&#46;e&#46;&#44; in HTML markup and in form submissions&#44; is intended to be computer&#45;readable and consistent irrespective of the user&#39;s locale&#46; Dates&#44; for instance&#44; are always written in the format &#34;YYYY&#45;MM&#45;DD&#34;&#44; as in &#34;2003&#45;02&#45;01&#34;&#46; While some users might see this format&#44; others might see it as &#34;01&#46;02&#46;2003&#34; or &#34;February 1&#44; 2003&#34;&#46;

The time&#44; date&#44; or number given by the page in the wire format is then translated to the user&#39;s preferred presentation &#40;based on user preferences or on the locale of the page itself&#41;&#44; before being displayed to the user&#46; Similarly&#44; after the user inputs a time&#44; date&#44; or number using their preferred format&#44; the user agent converts it back to the wire format before putting it in the DOM or submitting it&#46;

This allows scripts in pages and on servers to process times&#44; dates&#44; and numbers in a consistent manner without needing to support dozens of different formats&#44; while still supporting the users&#39; needs&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

See also the [implementation notes](#input-impl-notes) regarding localization of form controls&#46;

#### <a id="categories"></a>4&#46;10&#46;2 Categories[](#categories)

Mostly for historical reasons&#44; elements in this section fall into several overlapping &#40;but subtly different&#41; categories in addition to the usual ones like <a id="categories&#58;flow&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[flow content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#flow-content-2)&#44; <a id="categories&#58;phrasing&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[phrasing content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#phrasing-content-2)&#44; and <a id="categories&#58;interactive&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[interactive content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#interactive-content-2)&#46;

A number of the elements are <a id="form&#45;associated&#45;element"></a><strong>form&#45;associated elements</strong>&#44; which means they can have a <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;owner"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#46;

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;object&#45;element"></a><code>[object](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-object-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;output&#45;element"></a><code>[output](#the-output-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-img-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#form-associated-custom-element)

The <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated elements](#form-associated-element) fall into several subcategories&#58;

<strong><a id="category&#45;listed"></a><strong>Listed elements</strong></strong>

Denotes elements that are listed in the <a id="categories&#58;dom&#45;form&#45;elements"></a><code>[<var>form</var>&#46;elements](#dom-form-elements)</code> and <a id="categories&#58;dom&#45;fieldset&#45;elements"></a><code>[<var>fieldset</var>&#46;elements](#dom-fieldset-elements)</code> APIs&#46; These elements also have a <a id="categories&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> content attribute&#44; and a matching <a id="categories&#58;dom&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><code>[form](#dom-fae-form)</code> IDL attribute&#44; that allow authors to specify an explicit <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;2"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#46;

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;object&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[object](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-object-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;output&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[output](#the-output-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#form-associated-custom-element)

<strong><a id="category&#45;submit"></a><strong>Submittable elements</strong></strong>

Denotes elements that can be used for <a id="categories&#58;constructing&#45;the&#45;form&#45;data&#45;set"></a>[constructing the entry list](#constructing-the-form-data-set) when a <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element is <a id="categories&#58;concept&#45;form&#45;submit"></a>[submitted](#concept-form-submit)&#46;

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#form-associated-custom-element)

Some <a id="categories&#58;category&#45;submit"></a>[submittable elements](#category-submit) can be&#44; depending on their attributes&#44; <a id="concept&#45;button"></a><strong>buttons</strong>&#46; The prose below defines when an element is a button&#46; Some buttons are specifically <a id="concept&#45;submit&#45;button"></a><strong>submit buttons</strong>&#46;

<strong><a id="category&#45;reset"></a><strong>Resettable elements</strong></strong>

Denotes elements that can be affected when a <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element is <a id="categories&#58;concept&#45;form&#45;reset"></a>[reset](#concept-form-reset)&#46;

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;output&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[output](#the-output-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#form-associated-custom-element)

<strong><a id="category&#45;autocapitalize"></a><strong>Autocapitalize&#45;and&#45;autocorrect&#45;inheriting elements</strong></strong>

Denotes elements that inherit the <a id="categories&#58;attr&#45;autocapitalize"></a><code>[autocapitalize](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-autocapitalize)</code> and <a id="categories&#58;attr&#45;autocorrect"></a><code>[autocorrect](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-autocorrect)</code> attributes from their <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;3"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#46;

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;output&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[output](#the-output-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>

Some elements&#44; not all of them <a id="categories&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[form&#45;associated](#form-associated-element)&#44; are categorized as <a id="category&#45;label"></a><strong>labelable elements</strong>&#46; These are elements that can be associated with a <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element"></a><code>[label](#the-label-element)</code> element&#46;

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code>

- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code>
- <a id="categories&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>

``` text
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyOverrideBuiltIns,
 LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties]
interface HTMLFormElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect="accept-charset"] attribute DOMString acceptCharset;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute USVString action;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString autocomplete;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString enctype;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString encoding;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString method;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean noValidate;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString target;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString rel;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect="rel"] readonly attribute DOMTokenList relList;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLFormControlsCollection elements;
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter Element (unsigned long index);
  getter (RadioNodeList or Element) (DOMString name);

  undefined submit();
  undefined requestSubmit(optional HTMLElement? submitter = null);
  [CEReactions] undefined reset();
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
};
```

The <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;represents"></a>[represents](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#represents) a <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;hyperlink"></a>[hyperlink](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#hyperlink) that can be manipulated through a collection of <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated elements](#form-associated-element)&#44; some of which can represent editable values that can be submitted to a server for processing&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;form&#45;accept&#45;charset"></a><strong><code>accept&#45;charset</code></strong> attribute gives the character encodings that are to be used for the submission&#46; If specified&#44; the value must be an <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for &#34;<code>UTF&#45;8</code>&#34;&#46; [&#91;ENCODING&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsENCODING)

The <a id="attr&#45;form&#45;name"></a><strong><code>name</code></strong> attribute represents the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code>&#39;s name within the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;forms&#45;2"></a><code>[forms](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#dom-document-forms)</code> collection&#46; The value must not be the empty string&#44; and the value must be unique amongst the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> elements in the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;forms&#45;3"></a><code>[forms](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#dom-document-forms)</code> collection that it is in&#44; if any&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;form&#45;autocomplete"></a><strong><code>autocomplete</code></strong> attribute is an <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;enumerated&#45;attribute"></a>[enumerated attribute](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords and states&#58;

<table><thead><tr><th>Keyword      </th><th>State      </th><th>Brief description    </th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><dfn data-dfn-for="form/autocomplete" id="attr-form-autocomplete-on" data-dfn-type="attr-value"><code>on</code></dfn>      </td><td><dfn id="attr-form-autocomplete-on-state">On</dfn>      </td><td>Form controls will have their <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="the-form-element:autofill-field-name">autofill field name</a> set to &#34;<code id="the-form-element:attr-fe-autocomplete-on"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-on">on</a></code>&#34; by default&#46;     </td></tr><tr><td><dfn data-dfn-for="form/autocomplete" id="attr-form-autocomplete-off" data-dfn-type="attr-value"><code>off</code></dfn>      </td><td><dfn id="attr-form-autocomplete-off-state">Off</dfn>      </td><td>Form controls will have their <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="the-form-element:autofill-field-name-2">autofill field name</a> set to &#34;<code id="the-form-element:attr-fe-autocomplete-off"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-off">off</a></code>&#34; by default&#46;   </td></tr></tbody></table>

The attribute&#39;s <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;missing&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[missing value default](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#missing-value-default)</em> and <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;invalid&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[invalid value default](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#invalid-value-default)</em> are both the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;form&#45;autocomplete&#45;on&#45;state"></a>[On](#attr-form-autocomplete-on-state) state&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;action&#45;3"></a><code>[action](#attr-fs-action)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;enctype&#45;2"></a><code>[enctype](#attr-fs-enctype)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;method&#45;2"></a><code>[method](#attr-fs-method)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;novalidate&#45;2"></a><code>[novalidate](#attr-fs-novalidate)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;target&#45;2"></a><code>[target](#attr-fs-target)</code> attributes are <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attributes&#45;for&#45;form&#45;submission"></a>[attributes for form submission](#attributes-for-form-submission)&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;form&#45;rel"></a><strong><code>rel</code></strong> attribute on <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> elements controls what kinds of links the elements create&#46; The attribute&#39;s value must be a <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;unordered&#45;set&#45;of&#45;unique&#45;space&#45;separated&#45;tokens"></a>[unordered set of unique space&#45;separated tokens](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens)&#46; The [allowed keywords and their meanings](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#linkTypes) are defined in an earlier section&#46;

<a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;form&#45;rel&#45;3"></a><code>[rel](#attr-form-rel)</code>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;supported&#45;tokens"></a>[supported tokens](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens) are the keywords defined in [HTML link types](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#linkTypes) which are allowed on <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> elements&#44; impact the processing model&#44; and are supported by the user agent&#46; The possible <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;supported&#45;tokens&#45;2"></a>[supported tokens](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens) are <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;link&#45;type&#45;noreferrer"></a><code>[noreferrer](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#link-type-noreferrer)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;link&#45;type&#45;noopener"></a><code>[noopener](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#link-type-noopener)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;link&#45;type&#45;opener"></a><code>[opener](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#link-type-opener)</code>&#46; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;form&#45;rel&#45;4"></a><code>[rel](#attr-form-rel)</code>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;supported&#45;tokens&#45;3"></a>[supported tokens](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-supported-tokens) must only include the tokens from this list that the user agent implements the processing model for&#46;

<strong><code><var>form</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;form&#45;elements&#45;dev"></a>[elements](#dom-form-elements)</code></strong>

<strong><code><var>form</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;form&#45;length&#45;dev"></a>[length](#dom-form-length)</code></strong>

Returns the number of form controls in the form &#40;excluding image buttons for historical reasons&#41;&#46;

<strong><code><var>form</var>&#91;<var>index</var>&#93;</code></strong>

Returns the <var>index</var>th element in the form &#40;excluding image buttons for historical reasons&#41;&#46;

<strong><code><var>form</var>&#91;<var>name</var>&#93;</code></strong>

Returns the form control &#40;or&#44; if there are several&#44; a <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;radionodelist&#45;2"></a><code>[RadioNodeList](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#radionodelist)</code> of the form controls&#41; in the form with the given <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;id"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) or <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-name)</code> &#40;excluding image buttons for historical reasons&#41;&#59; or&#44; if there are none&#44; returns the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-img-element)</code> element with the given ID&#46;

Once an element has been referenced using a particular name&#44; that name will continue being available as a way to reference that element in this method&#44; even if the element&#39;s actual <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;2"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) or <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name&#45;2"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-name)</code> changes&#44; for as long as the element remains in the <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;tree"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#46;

If there are multiple matching items&#44; then a <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;radionodelist&#45;3"></a><code>[RadioNodeList](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#radionodelist)</code> object containing all those elements is returned&#46;

Requests to submit the form&#46; Unlike <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;form&#45;submit&#45;2"></a><code>[submit&#40;&#41;](#dom-form-submit)</code>&#44; this method includes <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;interactively&#45;validate&#45;the&#45;constraints&#45;2"></a>[interactive constraint validation](#interactively-validate-the-constraints) and firing a <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;event&#45;submit&#45;2"></a><code>[submit](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-submit)</code> event&#44; either of which can cancel submission&#46;

The <var>submitter</var> argument can be used to point to a specific <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;submit&#45;button"></a>[submit button](#concept-submit-button)&#44; whose <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;formaction"></a><code>[formaction](#attr-fs-formaction)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;formenctype"></a><code>[formenctype](#attr-fs-formenctype)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;formmethod"></a><code>[formmethod](#attr-fs-formmethod)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;formnovalidate"></a><code>[formnovalidate](#attr-fs-formnovalidate)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fs&#45;formtarget"></a><code>[formtarget](#attr-fs-formtarget)</code> attributes can impact submission&#46; Additionally&#44; the submitter will be included when <a id="the&#45;form&#45;element&#58;constructing&#45;the&#45;form&#45;data&#45;set"></a>[constructing the entry list](#constructing-the-form-data-set) for submission&#59; normally&#44; buttons are excluded&#46;
