The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;minlength"></a><strong><code>minlength</code></strong> attribute&#44; when it <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;apply&#45;2"></a>[applies](#concept-input-apply)&#44; is a <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;minlength"></a>[form control <code>minlength</code> attribute](#attr-fe-minlength)&#46;

If the <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element has a <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;maximum&#45;allowed&#45;value&#45;length"></a>[maximum allowed value length](#maximum-allowed-value-length)&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;length"></a>[length](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-length) of the value of the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;value"></a><code>[value](#attr-input-value)</code> attribute must be less than or equal to the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;maxlength&#45;and&#45;minlength&#45;attributes&#58;maximum&#45;allowed&#45;value&#45;length&#45;2"></a>[maximum allowed value length](#maximum-allowed-value-length)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following extract shows how a messaging client&#39;s text entry could be arbitrarily restricted to a fixed number of characters&#44; thus forcing any conversation through this medium to be terse and discouraging intelligent discourse&#46;

``` text
<label>What are you doing? <input name=status maxlength=140></label>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here&#44; a password is given a minimum length&#58;

``` text
<p><label>Username: <input name=u required></label>
<p><label>Password: <input name=p required minlength=12></label>
```

###### <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;2 The <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;size"></a><code>[size](#attr-input-size)</code> attribute[](#the-size-attribute)

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;size"></a><strong><code>size</code></strong> attribute gives the number of characters that&#44; in a visual rendering&#44; the user agent is to allow the user to see while editing the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;size&#45;2"></a><code>[size](#attr-input-size)</code> attribute&#44; if specified&#44; must have a value that is a <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;valid&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integer"></a>[valid non&#45;negative integer](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero&#46;

If the attribute is present&#44; then its value must be parsed using the <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integers"></a>[rules for parsing non&#45;negative integers](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers)&#44; and if the result is a number greater than zero&#44; then the user agent should ensure that at least that many characters are visible&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;dom&#45;input&#45;size"></a><code>[size](#dom-input-size)</code> IDL attribute is <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;limited&#45;to&#45;only&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;numbers&#45;greater&#45;than&#45;zero"></a>[limited to only positive numbers](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers-greater-than-zero) and has a <a id="the&#45;size&#45;attribute&#58;default&#45;value"></a>[default value](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#default-value) of 20&#46;

###### <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;3 The <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;readonly"></a><code>[readonly](#attr-input-readonly)</code> attribute[](#the-readonly-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Attributes&#47;readonly](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/readonly)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari1&#43;Chrome1&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer5&#46;5&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

[Attributes&#47;readonly](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/readonly)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome1&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer6&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

[Attributes&#47;readonly](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/readonly)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari≤4&#43;Chrome1&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera≤12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer≤6&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android≤12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;readonly"></a><strong><code>readonly</code></strong> attribute is a <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;boolean&#45;attribute"></a>[boolean attribute](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#boolean-attribute) that controls whether or not the user can edit the form control&#46; When specified&#44; the element is not <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;mutable"></a>[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; If the <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;readonly&#45;2"></a><code>[readonly](#attr-input-readonly)</code> attribute is specified on an <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; the element is <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;barred&#45;from&#45;constraint&#45;validation"></a>[barred from constraint validation](#barred-from-constraint-validation)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The difference between <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;disabled"></a><code>[disabled](#attr-fe-disabled)</code> and <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;readonly&#45;3"></a><code>[readonly](#attr-input-readonly)</code> is that read&#45;only controls can still function&#44; whereas disabled controls generally do not function as controls until they are enabled&#46; This is spelled out in more detail elsewhere in this specification with normative requirements that refer to the <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;disabled"></a>[disabled](#concept-fe-disabled) concept &#40;for example&#44; the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;activation&#45;behaviour"></a>[activation behavior](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior)&#44; whether or not it is a <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;focusable&#45;area"></a>[focusable area](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focusable-area)&#44; or when <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;constructing&#45;the&#45;form&#45;data&#45;set"></a>[constructing the entry list](#constructing-the-form-data-set)&#41;&#46; Any other behavior related to user interaction with disabled controls&#44; such as whether text can be selected or copied&#44; is not defined in this standard&#46;

Only text controls can be made read&#45;only&#44; since for other controls &#40;such as checkboxes and buttons&#41; there is no useful distinction between being read&#45;only and being disabled&#44; so the <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;readonly&#45;4"></a><code>[readonly](#attr-input-readonly)</code> attribute <a id="the&#45;readonly&#45;attribute&#58;do&#45;not&#45;apply"></a>[does not apply](#do-not-apply)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; the existing product identifiers cannot be modified&#44; but they are still displayed as part of the form&#44; for consistency with the row representing a new product &#40;where the identifier is not yet filled in&#41;&#46;

``` text
<form action="products.cgi" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
 <table>
  <tr> <th> Product ID <th> Product name <th> Price <th> Action
  <tr>
   <td> <input readonly="readonly" name="1.pid" value="H412">
   <td> <input required="required" name="1.pname" value="Floor lamp Ulke">
   <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="1.pprice" value="49.99">
   <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:1">Delete</button>
  <tr>
   <td> <input readonly="readonly" name="2.pid" value="FG28">
   <td> <input required="required" name="2.pname" value="Table lamp Ulke">
   <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="2.pprice" value="24.99">
   <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:2">Delete</button>
  <tr>
   <td> <input required="required" name="3.pid" value="" pattern="[A-Z0-9]+">
   <td> <input required="required" name="3.pname" value="">
   <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="3.pprice" value="">
   <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:3">Delete</button>
 </table>
 <p> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="add">Add</button> </p>
 <p> <button name="action" value="update">Save</button> </p>
</form>
```

###### <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;4 The <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;required"></a><code>[required](#attr-input-required)</code> attribute[](#the-required-attribute)

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;required"></a><strong><code>required</code></strong> attribute is a <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;boolean&#45;attribute"></a>[boolean attribute](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#boolean-attribute)&#46; When specified&#44; the element is <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;required"></a><strong><em>required</em></strong>&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; If the element is <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;required"></a><em>[required](#concept-input-required)</em>&#44; and its <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;dom&#45;input&#45;value"></a><code>[value](#dom-input-value)</code> IDL attribute <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;apply"></a>[applies](#concept-input-apply) and is in the mode <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;dom&#45;input&#45;value&#45;value"></a>[value](#dom-input-value-value)&#44; and the element is <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;mutable"></a>[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable)&#44; and the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is the empty string&#44; then the element is <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;being&#45;missing"></a>[suffering from being missing](#suffering-from-being-missing)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following form has two required fields&#44; one for an email address and one for a password&#46; It also has a third field that is only considered valid if the user types the same password in the password field and this third field&#46;

``` text
<h1>Create new account</h1>
<form action="/newaccount" method=post
      oninput="up2.setCustomValidity(up2.value != up.value ? 'Passwords do not match.' : '')">
 <p>
  <label for="username">Email address:</label>
  <input id="username" type=email required name=un>
 <p>
  <label for="password1">Password:</label>
  <input id="password1" type=password required name=up>
 <p>
  <label for="password2">Confirm password:</label>
  <input id="password2" type=password name=up2>
 <p>
  <input type=submit value="Create account">
</form>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For radio buttons&#44; the <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;required&#45;2"></a><code>[required](#attr-input-required)</code> attribute is satisfied if any of the radio buttons in the <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;radio&#45;button&#45;group"></a>[group](#radio-button-group) is selected&#46; Thus&#44; in the following example&#44; any of the radio buttons can be checked&#44; not just the one marked as required&#58;

``` text
<fieldset>
 <legend>Did the movie pass the Bechdel test?</legend>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-characters"> No, there are not even two female characters in the movie. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-names"> No, the female characters never talk to each other. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-topic"> No, when female characters talk to each other it's always about a male character. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="yes" required> Yes. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="unknown"> I don't know. </label>
</fieldset>
```

To avoid confusion as to whether a <a id="the&#45;required&#45;attribute&#58;radio&#45;button&#45;group&#45;2"></a>[radio button group](#radio-button-group) is required or not&#44; authors are encouraged to specify the attribute on all the radio buttons in a group&#46; Indeed&#44; in general&#44; authors are encouraged to avoid having radio button groups that do not have any initially checked controls in the first place&#44; as this is a state that the user cannot return to&#44; and is therefore generally considered a poor user interface&#46;

###### <a id="the&#45;multiple&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;5 The <a id="the&#45;multiple&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute[](#the-multiple-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Attributes&#47;multiple](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/multiple)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox3&#46;6&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome2&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

[Element&#47;input&#35;attr&#45;multiple](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#attr-multiple)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox3&#46;6&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome2&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera≤12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android≤37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android≤12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;multiple"></a><strong><code>multiple</code></strong> attribute is a <a id="the&#45;multiple&#45;attribute&#58;boolean&#45;attribute"></a>[boolean attribute](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#boolean-attribute) that indicates whether the user is to be allowed to specify more than one value&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following extract shows how an email client&#39;s &#34;To&#34; field could accept multiple email addresses&#46;

``` text
<label>To: <input type=email multiple name=to></label>
```

If the user had&#44; amongst many friends in their user contacts database&#44; two friends &#34;Spider&#45;Man&#34; &#40;with address &#34;spider&#64;parker&#46;example&#46;net&#34;&#41; and &#34;Scarlet Witch&#34; &#40;with address &#34;scarlet&#64;avengers&#46;example&#46;net&#34;&#41;&#44; then&#44; after the user has typed &#34;s&#34;&#44; the user agent might suggest these two email addresses to the user&#46;

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-email-1.svg)

The page could also link in the user&#39;s contacts database from the site&#58;

``` text
<label>To: <input type=email multiple name=to list=contacts></label>
...
<datalist id="contacts">
 <option value="hedral@damowmow.com">
 <option value="pillar@example.com">
 <option value="astrophy@cute.example">
 <option value="astronomy@science.example.org">
</datalist>
```

Suppose the user had entered &#34;bob&#64;example&#46;net&#34; into this text control&#44; and then started typing a second email address starting with &#34;s&#34;&#46; The user agent might show both the two friends mentioned earlier&#44; as well as the &#34;astrophy&#34; and &#34;astronomy&#34; values given in the <a id="the&#45;multiple&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element&#46;

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-email-2.svg)

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following extract shows how an email client&#39;s &#34;Attachments&#34; field could accept multiple files for upload&#46;

``` text
<label>Attachments: <input type=file multiple name=att></label>
```

###### <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;6 The <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;pattern"></a><code>[pattern](#attr-input-pattern)</code> attribute[](#the-pattern-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Attributes&#47;pattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/pattern)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari5&#43;Chrome4&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera≤12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS4&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android≤37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android≤12&#46;1&#43;

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Attributes&#47;pattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/pattern)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari5&#43;Chrome4&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS4&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;pattern"></a><strong><code>pattern</code></strong> attribute specifies a regular expression against which the control&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#44; or&#44; when the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;apply"></a>[applies](#concept-input-apply) and is set&#44; the control&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;values"></a>[values](#concept-fe-values)&#44; are to be checked&#46;

If specified&#44; the attribute&#39;s value must match the JavaScript <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;js&#45;prod&#45;pattern"></a><em>[Pattern](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-Pattern)</em><sub><code>&#91;&#43;UnicodeSetsMode&#44; &#43;N&#93;</code></sub> production&#46;

The <a id="compiled&#45;pattern&#45;regular&#45;expression"></a><strong>compiled pattern regular expression</strong> of an <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; if it exists&#44; is a JavaScript <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexp"></a><code>[RegExp](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexp-regular-expression-objects)</code> object&#46; It is determined as follows&#58;

1.  If the element does not have a <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;pattern&#45;2"></a><code>[pattern](#attr-input-pattern)</code> attribute specified&#44; then return nothing&#46; The element has no <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;compiled&#45;pattern&#45;regular&#45;expression"></a>[compiled pattern regular expression](#compiled-pattern-regular-expression)&#46;

2.  Let <var>pattern</var> be the value of the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;pattern&#45;3"></a><code>[pattern](#attr-input-pattern)</code> attribute of the element&#46;

3.  Let <var>regexpCompletion</var> be <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexpcreate"></a>[RegExpCreate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexpcreate)&#40;<var>pattern</var>&#44; &#34;<code>v</code>&#34;&#41;&#46;

4.  If <var>regexpCompletion</var> is an <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;completion&#45;record"></a>[abrupt completion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type)&#44; then return nothing&#46; The element has no <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;compiled&#45;pattern&#45;regular&#45;expression&#45;2"></a>[compiled pattern regular expression](#compiled-pattern-regular-expression)&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    User agents are encouraged to log this error in a developer console&#44; to aid debugging&#46;

5.  Let <var>anchoredPattern</var> be the string &#34;<code>&#94;&#40;&#63;&#58;</code>&#34;&#44; followed by <var>pattern</var>&#44; followed by &#34;<code>&#41;&#36;</code>&#34;&#46;

6.  Return &#33; <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexpcreate&#45;2"></a>[RegExpCreate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexpcreate)&#40;<var>anchoredPattern</var>&#44; &#34;<code>v</code>&#34;&#41;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The reasoning behind these steps&#44; instead of just using the value of the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;pattern&#45;4"></a><code>[pattern](#attr-input-pattern)</code> attribute directly&#44; is twofold&#46; First&#44; we want to ensure that when matched against a string&#44; the regular expression&#39;s start is anchored to the start of the string and its end to the end of the string&#46; Second&#44; we want to ensure that the regular expression is valid in standalone form&#44; instead of only becoming valid after being surrounded by the &#34;<code>&#94;&#40;&#63;&#58;</code>&#34; and &#34;<code>&#41;&#36;</code>&#34; anchors&#46;

A <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexp&#45;2"></a><code>[RegExp](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexp-regular-expression-objects)</code> object <var>regexp</var> <a id="regexp&#45;match&#45;a&#45;string"></a><strong>matches</strong> a string <var>input</var>&#44; if &#33; <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexpbuiltinexec"></a>[RegExpBuiltinExec](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexpbuiltinexec)&#40;<var>regexp</var>&#44; <var>input</var>&#41; is not null&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; If the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is not the empty string&#44; and either the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple&#45;2"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute is not specified or it <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;do&#45;not&#45;apply"></a>[does not apply](#do-not-apply) to the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element given its <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute&#39;s current state&#44; and the element has a <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;compiled&#45;pattern&#45;regular&#45;expression&#45;3"></a>[compiled pattern regular expression](#compiled-pattern-regular-expression) but that regular expression does not <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexp&#45;match&#45;a&#45;string"></a>[match](#regexp-match-a-string) the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#44; then the element is <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;a&#45;pattern&#45;mismatch"></a>[suffering from a pattern mismatch](#suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch)&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; If the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;4"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is not the empty string&#44; and the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple&#45;3"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute is specified and <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;apply&#45;2"></a>[applies](#concept-input-apply) to the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; and the element has a <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;compiled&#45;pattern&#45;regular&#45;expression&#45;4"></a>[compiled pattern regular expression](#compiled-pattern-regular-expression) but that regular expression does not <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;regexp&#45;match&#45;a&#45;string&#45;2"></a>[match](#regexp-match-a-string) each of the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;values&#45;2"></a>[values](#concept-fe-values)&#44; then the element is <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;a&#45;pattern&#45;mismatch&#45;2"></a>[suffering from a pattern mismatch](#suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch)&#46;

When an <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element has a <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;pattern&#45;5"></a><code>[pattern](#attr-input-pattern)</code> attribute specified&#44; authors should include a <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;title"></a><strong><code>title</code></strong> attribute to give a description of the pattern&#46; User agents may use the contents of this attribute&#44; if it is present&#44; when informing the user that the pattern is not matched&#44; or at any other suitable time&#44; such as in a tooltip or read out by assistive technology when the control <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;gains&#45;focus"></a>[gains focus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#gains-focus)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; the following snippet&#58;

``` text
<label> Part number:
 <input pattern="[0-9][A-Z]{3}" name="part"
        title="A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters."/>
</label>
```

&#46;&#46;&#46;could cause the UA to display an alert such as&#58;

``` text
A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters.
You cannot submit this form when the field is incorrect.
```

When a control has a <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;pattern&#45;6"></a><code>[pattern](#attr-input-pattern)</code> attribute&#44; the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;title"></a><code>[title](#attr-input-title)</code> attribute&#44; if used&#44; must describe the pattern&#46; Additional information could also be included&#44; so long as it assists the user in filling in the control&#46; Otherwise&#44; assistive technology would be impaired&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For instance&#44; if the title attribute contained the caption of the control&#44; assistive technology could end up saying something like <samp>The text you have entered does not match the required pattern&#46; Birthday</samp>&#44; which is not useful&#46;

UAs may still show the <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> in non&#45;error situations &#40;for example&#44; as a tooltip when hovering over the control&#41;&#44; so authors should be careful not to word <a id="the&#45;pattern&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;title&#45;2"></a><code>[title](#attr-input-title)</code>s as if an error has necessarily occurred&#46;

###### <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;7 The <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> and <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;max"></a><code>[max](#attr-input-max)</code> attributes[](#the-min-and-max-attributes)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Attributes&#47;max](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/max)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox16&#43;Safari5&#43;Chrome4&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS4&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

[Attributes&#47;min](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/min)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox16&#43;Safari5&#43;Chrome4&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS4&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

Some form controls can have explicit constraints applied limiting the allowed range of values that the user can provide&#46; Normally&#44; such a range would be linear and continuous&#46; A form control can <a id="has&#45;a&#45;periodic&#45;domain"></a><strong>have a periodic domain</strong>&#44; however&#44; in which case the form control&#39;s broadest possible range is finite&#44; and authors can specify explicit ranges within it that span the boundaries&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Specifically&#44; the broadest range of a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;time&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;time&#41;"></a><code>[type&#61;time](#time-state-(type=time))</code> control is midnight to midnight &#40;24 hours&#41;&#44; and authors can set both continuous linear ranges &#40;such as 9pm to 11pm&#41; and discontinuous ranges spanning midnight &#40;such as 11pm to 1am&#41;&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;min"></a><strong><code>min</code></strong> and <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;max"></a><strong><code>max</code></strong> attributes indicate the allowed range of values for the element&#46;

Their syntax is defined by the section that defines the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute&#39;s current state&#46;

If the element has a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min&#45;2"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> attribute&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min&#45;3"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> attribute is a number&#44; then that number is the element&#39;s <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;min"></a><strong>minimum</strong>&#59; otherwise&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;2"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute&#39;s current state defines a <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;default"></a><strong>default minimum</strong>&#44; then that is the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#59; otherwise&#44; the element has no <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;2"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min&#45;4"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> attribute also defines the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;zero"></a>[step base](#concept-input-min-zero)&#46;

If the element has a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;max&#45;2"></a><code>[max](#attr-input-max)</code> attribute&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number&#45;2"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;max&#45;3"></a><code>[max](#attr-input-max)</code> attribute is a number&#44; then that number is the element&#39;s <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;max"></a><strong>maximum</strong>&#59; otherwise&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;3"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute&#39;s current state defines a <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;default"></a><strong>default maximum</strong>&#44; then that is the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max)&#59; otherwise&#44; the element has no <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;2"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max)&#46;

If the element does not <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;has&#45;a&#45;periodic&#45;domain"></a>[have a periodic domain](#has-a-periodic-domain)&#44; the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;max&#45;4"></a><code>[max](#attr-input-max)</code> attribute&#39;s value &#40;the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;3"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max)&#41; must not be less than the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min&#45;5"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> attribute&#39;s value &#40;its <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;3"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#41;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

If an element that does not <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;has&#45;a&#45;periodic&#45;domain&#45;2"></a>[have a periodic domain](#has-a-periodic-domain) has a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;4"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max) that is less than its <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;4"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#44; then so long as the element has a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#44; it will either be <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;underflow"></a>[suffering from an underflow](#suffering-from-an-underflow) or <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;overflow"></a>[suffering from an overflow](#suffering-from-an-overflow)&#46;

An element <a id="has&#45;a&#45;reversed&#45;range"></a><strong>has a reversed range</strong> if it <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;has&#45;a&#45;periodic&#45;domain&#45;3"></a>[has a periodic domain](#has-a-periodic-domain) and its <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;5"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max) is less than its <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;5"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#46;

An element <a id="have&#45;range&#45;limitations"></a><strong>has range limitations</strong> if it has a defined <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;6"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min) or a defined <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;6"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max)&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; When the element has a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;7"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min) and does not <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;has&#45;a&#45;reversed&#45;range"></a>[have a reversed range](#has-a-reversed-range)&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number&#45;3"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is a number&#44; and the number obtained from that algorithm is less than the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;8"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#44; the element is <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;underflow&#45;2"></a>[suffering from an underflow](#suffering-from-an-underflow)&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; When the element has a <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;7"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max) and does not <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;has&#45;a&#45;reversed&#45;range&#45;2"></a>[have a reversed range](#has-a-reversed-range)&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number&#45;4"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is a number&#44; and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;8"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max)&#44; the element is <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;overflow&#45;2"></a>[suffering from an overflow](#suffering-from-an-overflow)&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; When an element <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;has&#45;a&#45;reversed&#45;range&#45;3"></a>[has a reversed range](#has-a-reversed-range)&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number&#45;5"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;4"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is a number&#44; and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;max&#45;9"></a>[maximum](#concept-input-max) <em>and</em> less than the <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;9"></a>[minimum](#concept-input-min)&#44; the element is simultaneously <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;underflow&#45;3"></a>[suffering from an underflow](#suffering-from-an-underflow) and <a id="the&#45;min&#45;and&#45;max&#45;attributes&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;overflow&#45;3"></a>[suffering from an overflow](#suffering-from-an-overflow)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following date control limits input to dates that are before the 1980s&#58;

``` text
<input name=bday type=date max="1979-12-31">
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following number control limits input to whole numbers greater than zero&#58;

``` text
<input name=quantity required="" type="number" min="1" value="1">
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following time control limits input to those minutes that occur between 9pm and 6am&#44; defaulting to midnight&#58;

``` text
<input name="sleepStart" type=time min="21:00" max="06:00" step="60" value="00:00">
```

###### <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;8 The <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;step"></a><code>[step](#attr-input-step)</code> attribute[](#the-step-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Attributes&#47;step](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/step)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox16&#43;Safari5&#43;Chrome5&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS4&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;step"></a><strong><code>step</code></strong> attribute indicates the granularity that is expected &#40;and required&#41; of the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) or <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;values"></a>[values](#concept-fe-values)&#44; by limiting the allowed values&#46; The section that defines the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute&#39;s current state also defines the <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;default"></a><strong>default step</strong>&#44; the <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;scale"></a><strong>step scale factor</strong>&#44; and in some cases the <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;default&#45;base"></a><strong>default step base</strong>&#44; which are used in processing the attribute as described below&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;step&#45;2"></a><code>[step](#attr-input-step)</code> attribute&#44; if specified&#44; must either have a value that is a <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a>[valid floating&#45;point number](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-floating-point-number) that <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values"></a>[parses](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to a number that is greater than zero&#44; or must have a value that is an <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string &#34;<code>any</code>&#34;&#46;

The attribute provides the <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;step"></a><strong>allowed value step</strong> for the element&#44; as follows&#58;

1.  If the attribute does not <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;apply"></a>[apply](#concept-input-apply)&#44; then there is no <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step)&#46;

2.  Otherwise&#44; if the attribute is absent&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;2"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step) is the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;default"></a>[default step](#concept-input-step-default) multiplied by the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;scale"></a>[step scale factor](#concept-input-step-scale)&#46;

3.  Otherwise&#44; if the attribute&#39;s value is an <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive&#45;2"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string &#34;<code>any</code>&#34;&#44; then there is no <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;3"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step)&#46;

4.  Otherwise&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values&#45;2"></a>[rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values)&#44; when they are applied to the attribute&#39;s value&#44; return an error&#44; zero&#44; or a number less than zero&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;4"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step) is the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;default&#45;2"></a>[default step](#concept-input-step-default) multiplied by the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;scale&#45;2"></a>[step scale factor](#concept-input-step-scale)&#46;

5.  Otherwise&#44; the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;5"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step) is the number returned by the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values&#45;3"></a>[rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) when they are applied to the attribute&#39;s value&#44; multiplied by the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;scale&#45;3"></a>[step scale factor](#concept-input-step-scale)&#46;

The <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;zero"></a><strong>step base</strong> is the value returned by the following algorithm&#58;

1.  If the element has a <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> content attribute&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;min&#45;2"></a><code>[min](#attr-input-min)</code> content attribute is not an error&#44; then return that result&#46;

2.  If the element has a <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;value"></a><code>[value](#attr-input-value)</code> content attribute&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number&#45;2"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;value&#45;2"></a><code>[value](#attr-input-value)</code> content attribute is not an error&#44; then return that result&#46;

3.  If a <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;default&#45;base"></a>[default step base](#concept-input-step-default-base) is defined for this element given its <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type&#45;2"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute&#39;s state&#44; then return it&#46;

4.  Return zero&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; When the element has an <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;6"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step)&#44; and the result of applying the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;string&#45;number&#45;3"></a>[algorithm to convert a string to a number](#concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is a number&#44; and that number subtracted from the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;min&#45;zero"></a>[step base](#concept-input-min-zero) is not an integral multiple of the <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;step&#45;7"></a>[allowed value step](#concept-input-step)&#44; the element is <a id="the&#45;step&#45;attribute&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;a&#45;step&#45;mismatch"></a>[suffering from a step mismatch](#suffering-from-a-step-mismatch)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following range control only accepts values in the range 0&#46;&#46;1&#44; and allows 256 steps in that range&#58;

``` text
<input name=opacity type=range min=0 max=1 step=0.00392156863>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following control allows any time in the day to be selected&#44; with any accuracy &#40;e&#46;g&#46; thousandth&#45;of&#45;a&#45;second accuracy or more&#41;&#58;

``` text
<input name=favtime type=time step=any>
```

Normally&#44; time controls are limited to an accuracy of one minute&#46;

###### <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;9 The <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;list"></a><code>[list](#attr-input-list)</code> attribute[](#the-list-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Element&#47;input&#35;list](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#list)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari12&#46;1&#43;Chrome20&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android4&#46;4&#46;3&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;list"></a><strong><code>list</code></strong> attribute is used to identify an element that lists predefined options suggested to the user&#46;

If present&#44; its value must be the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;id"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) of a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element in the same <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;tree"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#46;

The <a id="concept&#45;input&#45;list"></a><strong>suggestions source element</strong> is the first element in the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;tree&#45;2"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree) in <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;tree&#45;order"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order) to have an <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;2"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) equal to the value of the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;list&#45;2"></a><code>[list](#attr-input-list)</code> attribute&#44; if that element is a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element&#46; If there is no <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;list&#45;3"></a><code>[list](#attr-input-list)</code> attribute&#44; or if there is no element with that <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;3"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id)&#44; or if the first element with that <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;4"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) is not a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element&#44; then there is no <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;list"></a>[suggestions source element](#concept-input-list)&#46;

If there is a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;list&#45;2"></a>[suggestions source element](#concept-input-list)&#44; then&#44; when the user agent is allowing the user to edit the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#44; the user agent should offer the suggestions represented by the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;list&#45;3"></a>[suggestions source element](#concept-input-list) to the user in a manner suitable for the type of control used&#46; If appropriate&#44; the user agent should use the suggestion&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;label"></a>[label](#concept-option-label) and <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-option-value) to identify the suggestion to the user&#46;

User agents are encouraged to filter the suggestions represented by the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;list&#45;4"></a>[suggestions source element](#concept-input-list) when the number of suggestions is large&#44; including only the most relevant ones &#40;e&#46;g&#46; based on the user&#39;s input so far&#41;&#46; No precise threshold is defined&#44; but capping the list at four to seven values is reasonable&#46; If filtering based on the user&#39;s input&#44; user agents should search within both the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;label&#45;2"></a>[label](#concept-option-label) and <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-option-value) of the suggestions for matches&#46; User agents should consider how input variations affect the matching process&#46; Unicode normalization should be applied so that different underlying Unicode code point sequences&#44; caused by different keyboard&#45; or input&#45;specific mechanisms&#44; do not interfere with the matching process&#46; Case variations should be ignored&#44; which may require language&#45;specific case mapping&#46; For examples of these&#44; see Character Model for the World Wide Web&#58; String Matching&#46; User agents may also provide other matching features&#58; for illustration&#44; a few examples include matching different forms of kana to each other &#40;or to kanji&#41;&#44; ignoring accents&#44; or applying spelling correction&#46; [&#91;CHARMODNORM&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCHARMODNORM)

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This text field allows you to choose a type of JavaScript function&#46;

``` text
<input type="text" list="function-types">
<datalist id="function-types">
  <option value="function">function</option>
  <option value="async function">async function</option>
  <option value="function*">generator function</option>
  <option value="=>">arrow function</option>
  <option value="async =>">async arrow function</option>
  <option value="async function*">async generator function</option>
</datalist>
```

For user agents that follow the above suggestions&#44; both the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;label&#45;3"></a>[label](#concept-option-label) and <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](#concept-option-value) would be shown&#58;

![A text box with a drop down button on the right hand side&#59; with&#44; below&#44; a drop down box containing a list of the six values the left and the six labels on the right&#46;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-datalist.svg)

Then&#44; typing &#34;arrow&#34; or &#34;&#61;&#62;&#34; would filter the list to the entries with labels &#34;arrow function&#34; and &#34;async arrow function&#34;&#46; Typing &#34;generator&#34; or &#34;&#42;&#34; would filter the list to the entries with labels &#34;generator function&#34; and &#34;async generator function&#34;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

As always&#44; user agents are free to make user interface decisions which are appropriate for their particular requirements and for the user&#39;s particular circumstances&#46; However&#44; this has historically been an area of confusion for implementers&#44; web developers&#44; and users alike&#44; so we&#39;ve given some &#34;should&#34; suggestions above&#46;

How user selections of suggestions are handled depends on whether the element is a control accepting a single value only&#44; or whether it accepts multiple values&#58;

<strong>If the element does not have a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute specified or if the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple&#45;2"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;do&#45;not&#45;apply"></a>[does not apply](#do-not-apply)</strong>

When the user selects a suggestion&#44; the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) must be set to the selected suggestion&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;value&#45;4"></a>[value](#concept-option-value)&#44; as if the user had written that value themself&#46;

<strong>If the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute is in the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;email&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;email&#41;"></a>[Email](#email-state-(type=email)) state and the element has a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple&#45;3"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute specified</strong>

When the user selects a suggestion&#44; the user agent must either add a new entry to the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;values"></a>[values](#concept-fe-values)&#44; whose value is the selected suggestion&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;value&#45;5"></a>[value](#concept-option-value)&#44; or change an existing entry in the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;values&#45;2"></a>[values](#concept-fe-values) to have the value given by the selected suggestion&#39;s <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;value&#45;6"></a>[value](#concept-option-value)&#44; as if the user had themself added an entry with that value&#44; or edited an existing entry to be that value&#46; Which behavior is to be applied depends on the user interface in an <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;implementation&#45;defined"></a>[implementation&#45;defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) manner&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

If the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;list&#45;4"></a><code>[list](#attr-input-list)</code> attribute <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;do&#45;not&#45;apply&#45;2"></a>[does not apply](#do-not-apply)&#44; there is no <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;list&#45;5"></a>[suggestions source element](#concept-input-list)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This URL field offers some suggestions&#46;

``` text
<label>Homepage: <input name=hp type=url list=hpurls></label>
<datalist id=hpurls>
 <option value="https://www.google.com/" label="Google">
 <option value="https://www.reddit.com/" label="Reddit">
</datalist>
```

Other URLs from the user&#39;s history might show also&#59; this is up to the user agent&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This example demonstrates how to design a form that uses the autocompletion list feature while still degrading usefully in legacy user agents&#46;

If the autocompletion list is merely an aid&#44; and is not important to the content&#44; then simply using a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element with children <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> elements is enough&#46; To prevent the values from being rendered in legacy user agents&#44; they need to be placed inside the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;option&#45;value"></a><code>[value](#attr-option-value)</code> attribute instead of inline&#46;

``` text
<p>
 <label>
  Enter a breed:
  <input type="text" name="breed" list="breeds">
  <datalist id="breeds">
   <option value="Abyssinian">
   <option value="Alpaca">
   <!-- ... -->
  </datalist>
 </label>
</p>
```

However&#44; if the values need to be shown in legacy UAs&#44; then fallback content can be placed inside the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element&#44; as follows&#58;

``` text
<p>
 <label>
  Enter a breed:
  <input type="text" name="breed" list="breeds">
 </label>
 <datalist id="breeds">
  <label>
   or select one from the list:
   <select name="breed">
    <option value=""> (none selected)
    <option>Abyssinian
    <option>Alpaca
    <!-- ... -->
   </select>
  </label>
 </datalist>
</p>
```

The fallback content will only be shown in UAs that don&#39;t support <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code>&#46; The options&#44; on the other hand&#44; will be detected by all UAs&#44; even though they are not children of the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> element&#46;

Note that if an <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element used in a <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code> is <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;option&#45;selected"></a><code>[selected](#attr-option-selected)</code>&#44; it will be selected by default by legacy UAs &#40;because it affects the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#41;&#44; but it will not have any effect on the <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element in UAs that support <a id="the&#45;list&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;datalist&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[datalist](#the-datalist-element)</code>&#46;

###### <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;3&#46;10 The <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;placeholder"></a><code>[placeholder](#attr-input-placeholder)</code> attribute[](#the-placeholder-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Element&#47;input&#35;placeholder](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#placeholder)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome3&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

[Element&#47;input&#35;attr&#45;placeholder](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#attr-placeholder)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox4&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome3&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera≤12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android≤37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android≤12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;input&#45;placeholder"></a><strong><code>placeholder</code></strong> attribute represents a <em>short</em> hint &#40;a word or short phrase&#41; intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value&#46; A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format&#46; The attribute&#44; if specified&#44; must have a value that contains no U&#43;000A LINE FEED &#40;LF&#41; or U&#43;000D CARRIAGE RETURN &#40;CR&#41; characters&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;placeholder&#45;2"></a><code>[placeholder](#attr-input-placeholder)</code> attribute should not be used as an alternative to a <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element"></a><code>[label](#the-label-element)</code>&#46; For a longer hint or other advisory text&#44; the <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute is more appropriate&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

These mechanisms are very similar but subtly different&#58; the hint given by the control&#39;s <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[label](#the-label-element)</code> is shown at all times&#59; the short hint given in the <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;placeholder&#45;3"></a><code>[placeholder](#attr-input-placeholder)</code> attribute is shown before the user enters a value&#59; and the hint in the <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;title&#45;2"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute is shown when the user requests further help&#46;

User agents should present this hint to the user&#44; after having <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;strip&#45;newlines"></a>[stripped newlines](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-newlines) from it&#44; when the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is the empty string&#44; especially if the control is not <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;focused"></a>[focused](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focused)&#46;

If a user agent normally doesn&#39;t show this hint to the user when the control is <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;focused&#45;2"></a>[focused](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focused)&#44; then the user agent should nonetheless show the hint for the control if it was focused as a result of the <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autofocus"></a><code>[autofocus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-fe-autofocus)</code> attribute&#44; since in that case the user will not have had an opportunity to examine the control before focusing it&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here is an example of a mail configuration user interface that uses the <a id="the&#45;placeholder&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;placeholder&#45;4"></a><code>[placeholder](#attr-input-placeholder)</code> attribute&#58;

``` text
<fieldset>
 <legend>Mail Account</legend>
 <p><label>Name: <input type="text" name="fullname" placeholder="John Ratzenberger"></label></p>
 <p><label>Address: <input type="email" name="address" placeholder="john@example.net"></label></p>
 <p><label>Password: <input type="password" name="password"></label></p>
 <p><label>Description: <input type="text" name="desc" placeholder="My Email Account"></label></p>
</fieldset>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In situations where the control&#39;s content has one directionality but the placeholder needs to have a different directionality&#44; Unicode&#39;s bidirectional&#45;algorithm formatting characters can be used in the attribute value&#58;

``` text
<input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B; رقم الهاتف 1 &#x202E;">
<input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B; رقم الهاتف 2 &#x202E;">
```

For slightly more clarity&#44; here&#39;s the same example using numeric character references instead of inline Arabic&#58;

``` text
<input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 1&#x202E;">
<input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 2&#x202E;">
```

##### <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis"></a>4&#46;10&#46;5&#46;4 Common <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element APIs[](#common-input-element-apis)

<strong><code><var>input</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;input&#45;value&#45;dev"></a>[value](#dom-input-value) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns the current <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) of the form control&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the value&#46;

Throws an <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;invalidstateerror"></a>[&#34;<code>InvalidStateError</code>&#34;](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;domexception"></a><code>[DOMException](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException)</code> if it is set to any value other than the empty string when the control is a file upload control&#46;

<strong><code><var>input</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;input&#45;checked&#45;dev"></a>[checked](#dom-input-checked) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns the current <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;checked"></a>[checkedness](#concept-fe-checked) of the form control&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;checked&#45;2"></a>[checkedness](#concept-fe-checked)&#46;

<strong><code><var>input</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;input&#45;files&#45;dev"></a>[files](#dom-input-files) &#91; &#61; <var>files</var> &#93;</code></strong>

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[FileList](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FileList)

Support in all current engines&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android11&#46;1&#43;

[HTMLInputElement&#47;files](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement/files)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox3&#43;Safari4&#43;Chrome2&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer🔰 10&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS3&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android37&#43;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

Returns a <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;filelist"></a><code>[FileList](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section)</code> object listing the <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;type&#45;file&#45;selected"></a>[selected files](#concept-input-type-file-selected) of the form control&#46;

Returns null if the control isn&#39;t a file control&#46;

Can be set to a <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;filelist&#45;2"></a><code>[FileList](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section)</code> object to change the <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;type&#45;file&#45;selected&#45;2"></a>[selected files](#concept-input-type-file-selected) of the form control&#46; For instance&#44; as the result of a drag&#45;and&#45;drop operation&#46;

<strong><code><var>input</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;input&#45;valueasdate&#45;dev"></a>[valueAsDate](#dom-input-valueasdate) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns a <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;date"></a><code>[Date](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects)</code> object representing the form control&#39;s <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#44; if applicable&#59; otherwise&#44; returns null&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the value&#46;

Throws an <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;invalidstateerror&#45;2"></a>[&#34;<code>InvalidStateError</code>&#34;](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;domexception&#45;2"></a><code>[DOMException](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException)</code> if the control isn&#39;t date&#45; or time&#45;based&#46;

<strong><code><var>input</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;input&#45;valueasnumber&#45;dev"></a>[valueAsNumber](#dom-input-valueasnumber) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns a number representing the form control&#39;s <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#44; if applicable&#59; otherwise&#44; returns NaN&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the value&#46; Setting this to NaN will set the underlying value to the empty string&#46;

Throws an <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;invalidstateerror&#45;3"></a>[&#34;<code>InvalidStateError</code>&#34;](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) <a id="common&#45;input&#45;element&#45;apis&#58;domexception&#45;3"></a><code>[DOMException](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException)</code> if the control is neither date&#45; or time&#45;based nor numeric&#46;

<strong><code><var>input</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;input&#45;stepup&#45;dev"></a>[stepUp](#dom-input-stepup)&#40;&#91; <var>n</var> &#93;&#41;</code></strong>
