[Attributes&#47;min](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/min)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox16&#43;Safari6&#43;Chrome6&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera11&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;18Internet ExplorerNo

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS10&#46;3&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView AndroidNoSamsung Internet&#63;Opera Android11&#43;

The <a id="attr&#45;meter&#45;min"></a><strong><code>min</code></strong> attribute specifies the lower bound of the range&#44; and the <a id="attr&#45;meter&#45;max"></a><strong><code>max</code></strong> attribute specifies the upper bound&#46; The <a id="attr&#45;meter&#45;value"></a><strong><code>value</code></strong> attribute specifies the value to have the gauge indicate as the &#34;measured&#34; value&#46;

The other three attributes can be used to segment the gauge&#39;s range into &#34;low&#34;&#44; &#34;medium&#34;&#44; and &#34;high&#34; parts&#44; and to indicate which part of the gauge is the &#34;optimum&#34; part&#46; The <a id="attr&#45;meter&#45;low"></a><strong><code>low</code></strong> attribute specifies the range that is considered to be the &#34;low&#34; part&#44; and the <a id="attr&#45;meter&#45;high"></a><strong><code>high</code></strong> attribute specifies the range that is considered to be the &#34;high&#34; part&#46; The <a id="attr&#45;meter&#45;optimum"></a><strong><code>optimum</code></strong> attribute gives the position that is &#34;optimum&#34;&#59; if that is higher than the &#34;high&#34; value then this indicates that the higher the value&#44; the better&#59; if it&#39;s lower than the &#34;low&#34; mark then it indicates that lower values are better&#44; and naturally if it is in between then it indicates that neither high nor low values are good&#46;

<strong>Authoring requirements</strong>&#58; The <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;value&#45;2"></a><code>[value](#attr-meter-value)</code> attribute must be specified&#46; The <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;value&#45;3"></a><code>[value](#attr-meter-value)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;min&#45;2"></a><code>[min](#attr-meter-min)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;2"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;2"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;max&#45;2"></a><code>[max](#attr-meter-max)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;optimum&#45;2"></a><code>[optimum](#attr-meter-optimum)</code> attributes&#44; when present&#44; must have values that are <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a>[valid floating&#45;point numbers](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-floating-point-number)&#46;

In addition&#44; the attributes&#39; values are further constrained&#58;

Let <var>value</var> be the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;value&#45;4"></a><code>[value](#attr-meter-value)</code> attribute&#39;s number&#46;

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;min&#45;3"></a><code>[min](#attr-meter-min)</code> attribute is specified&#44; then let <var>minimum</var> be that attribute&#39;s value&#59; otherwise&#44; let it be 0&#46;

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;max&#45;3"></a><code>[max](#attr-meter-max)</code> attribute is specified&#44; then let <var>maximum</var> be that attribute&#39;s value&#59; otherwise&#44; let it be 1&#46;0&#46;

The following inequalities must hold&#44; as applicable&#58;

- <var>minimum</var> ≤ <var>value</var> ≤ <var>maximum</var>

- <var>minimum</var> ≤ <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;3"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code> ≤ <var>maximum</var> &#40;if <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;4"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code> is specified&#41;

- <var>minimum</var> ≤ <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;3"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code> ≤ <var>maximum</var> &#40;if <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;4"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code> is specified&#41;

- <var>minimum</var> ≤ <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;optimum&#45;3"></a><code>[optimum](#attr-meter-optimum)</code> ≤ <var>maximum</var> &#40;if <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;optimum&#45;4"></a><code>[optimum](#attr-meter-optimum)</code> is specified&#41;

- <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;5"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code> ≤ <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;5"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code> &#40;if both <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;6"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code> and <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;6"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code> are specified&#41;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

If no minimum or maximum is specified&#44; then the range is assumed to be 0&#46;&#46;1&#44; and the value thus has to be within that range&#46;

Authors are encouraged to include a textual representation of the gauge&#39;s state in the element&#39;s contents&#44; for users of user agents that do not support the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;the&#45;meter&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[meter](#the-meter-element)</code> element&#46;

When used with <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;microdata"></a>[microdata](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#microdata)&#44; the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;the&#45;meter&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[meter](#the-meter-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;value&#45;5"></a><code>[value](#attr-meter-value)</code> attribute provides the element&#39;s machine&#45;readable value&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following examples show three gauges that would all be three&#45;quarters full&#58;

``` text
Storage space usage: <meter value=6 max=8>6 blocks used (out of 8 total)</meter>
```

``` text
Voter turnout: <meter value=0.75><img alt="75%" src="graph75.png"></meter>
```

``` text
Tickets sold: <meter min="0" max="100" value="75"></meter>
```

The following example is incorrect use of the element&#44; because it doesn&#39;t give a range &#40;and since the default maximum is 1&#44; both of the gauges would end up looking maxed out&#41;&#58;

``` text
<p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of <meter value=12>12cm</meter>
and a height of <meter value=2>2cm</meter>.</p> <!-- BAD! -->
```

Instead&#44; one would either not include the meter element&#44; or use the meter element with a defined range to give the dimensions in context compared to other pies&#58;

``` text
<p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of 12cm and a height of
2cm.</p>
<dl>
 <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12>12cm</meter>
 <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2>2cm</meter>
</dl>
```

There is no explicit way to specify units in the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;the&#45;meter&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[meter](#the-meter-element)</code> element&#44; but the units may be specified in the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute in free&#45;form text&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The example above could be extended to mention the units&#58;

``` text
<dl>
 <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12 title="centimeters">12cm</meter>
 <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2 title="centimeters">2cm</meter>
</dl>
```

<strong>User agent requirements</strong>&#58; User agents must parse the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;min&#45;4"></a><code>[min](#attr-meter-min)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;max&#45;4"></a><code>[max](#attr-meter-max)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;value&#45;6"></a><code>[value](#attr-meter-value)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;7"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;7"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;optimum&#45;5"></a><code>[optimum](#attr-meter-optimum)</code> attributes using the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values"></a>[rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values)&#46;

User agents must then use all these numbers to obtain values for six points on the gauge&#44; as follows&#46; &#40;The order in which these are evaluated is important&#44; as some of the values refer to earlier ones&#46;&#41;

<strong>The <a id="concept&#45;meter&#45;minimum"></a><strong>minimum value</strong></strong>

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;min&#45;5"></a><code>[min](#attr-meter-min)</code> attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it&#44; then the minimum value is that value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the minimum value is zero&#46;

<strong>The <a id="concept&#45;meter&#45;maximum"></a><strong>maximum value</strong></strong>

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;max&#45;5"></a><code>[max](#attr-meter-max)</code> attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it&#44; then the candidate maximum value is that value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the candidate maximum value is 1&#46;0&#46;

If the candidate maximum value is greater than or equal to the minimum value&#44; then the maximum value is the candidate maximum value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the maximum value is the same as the minimum value&#46;

<strong>The <a id="concept&#45;meter&#45;actual"></a><strong>actual value</strong></strong>

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;value&#45;7"></a><code>[value](#attr-meter-value)</code> attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it&#44; then that value is the candidate actual value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the candidate actual value is zero&#46;

If the candidate actual value is less than the minimum value&#44; then the actual value is the minimum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; if the candidate actual value is greater than the maximum value&#44; then the actual value is the maximum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; the actual value is the candidate actual value&#46;

<strong>The <a id="concept&#45;meter&#45;low"></a><strong>low boundary</strong></strong>

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;low&#45;8"></a><code>[low](#attr-meter-low)</code> attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it&#44; then the candidate low boundary is that value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the candidate low boundary is the same as the minimum value&#46;

If the candidate low boundary is less than the minimum value&#44; then the low boundary is the minimum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; if the candidate low boundary is greater than the maximum value&#44; then the low boundary is the maximum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; the low boundary is the candidate low boundary&#46;

<strong>The <a id="concept&#45;meter&#45;high"></a><strong>high boundary</strong></strong>

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;high&#45;8"></a><code>[high](#attr-meter-high)</code> attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it&#44; then the candidate high boundary is that value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the candidate high boundary is the same as the maximum value&#46;

If the candidate high boundary is less than the low boundary&#44; then the high boundary is the low boundary&#46;

Otherwise&#44; if the candidate high boundary is greater than the maximum value&#44; then the high boundary is the maximum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; the high boundary is the candidate high boundary&#46;

<strong>The <a id="concept&#45;meter&#45;optimum"></a><strong>optimum point</strong></strong>

If the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;meter&#45;optimum&#45;6"></a><code>[optimum](#attr-meter-optimum)</code> attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it&#44; then the candidate optimum point is that value&#46; Otherwise&#44; the candidate optimum point is the midpoint between the minimum value and the maximum value&#46;

If the candidate optimum point is less than the minimum value&#44; then the optimum point is the minimum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; if the candidate optimum point is greater than the maximum value&#44; then the optimum point is the maximum value&#46;

Otherwise&#44; the optimum point is the candidate optimum point&#46;

All of which will result in the following inequalities all being true&#58;

- minimum value ≤ actual value ≤ maximum value

- minimum value ≤ low boundary ≤ high boundary ≤ maximum value

- minimum value ≤ optimum point ≤ maximum value

<strong>UA requirements for regions of the gauge</strong>&#58; If the optimum point is equal to the low boundary or the high boundary&#44; or anywhere in between them&#44; then the region between the low and high boundaries of the gauge must be treated as the optimum region&#44; and the low and high parts&#44; if any&#44; must be treated as suboptimal&#46; Otherwise&#44; if the optimum point is less than the low boundary&#44; then the region between the minimum value and the low boundary must be treated as the optimum region&#44; the region from the low boundary up to the high boundary must be treated as a suboptimal region&#44; and the remaining region must be treated as an even less good region&#46; Finally&#44; if the optimum point is higher than the high boundary&#44; then the situation is reversed&#59; the region between the high boundary and the maximum value must be treated as the optimum region&#44; the region from the high boundary down to the low boundary must be treated as a suboptimal region&#44; and the remaining region must be treated as an even less good region&#46;

<strong>UA requirements for showing the gauge</strong>&#58; When representing a <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;the&#45;meter&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[meter](#the-meter-element)</code> element to the user&#44; the UA should indicate the relative position of the actual value to the minimum and maximum values&#44; and the relationship between the actual value and the three regions of the gauge&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following markup&#58;

``` text
<h3>Suggested groups</h3>
<menu>
 <li><a href="?cmd=hsg" onclick="hideSuggestedGroups()">Hide suggested groups</a></li>
</menu>
<ul>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/view">comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets</a> -
     <a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p>Group description: <strong>Layout/presentation on the WWW.</strong></p>
  <p><meter value="0.5">Moderate activity,</meter> Usenet, 618 subscribers</p>
 </li>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/view">netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall</a> -
     <a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p>Group description: <strong>Mozilla XPInstall discussion.</strong></p>
  <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 22 subscribers</p>
 </li>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/view">mozilla.dev.general</a> -
     <a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 66 subscribers</p>
 </li>
</ul>
```

Might be rendered as follows&#58;

![With the &#60;meter&#62; elements rendered as inline green bars of varying lengths&#46;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-meter.png)

User agents may combine the value of the <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;title&#45;2"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute and the other attributes to provide context&#45;sensitive help or inline text detailing the actual values&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; the following snippet&#58;

``` text
<meter min=0 max=60 value=23.2 title=seconds></meter>
```

&#46;&#46;&#46;might cause the user agent to display a gauge with a tooltip saying &#34;Value&#58; 23&#46;2 out of 60&#46;&#34; on one line and &#34;seconds&#34; on a second line&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;meter&#45;value"></a><strong><code>value</code></strong> getter steps are to return <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;this"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;meter&#45;actual"></a>[actual value](#concept-meter-actual)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;meter&#45;min"></a><strong><code>min</code></strong> getter steps are to return <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;this&#45;2"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;meter&#45;minimum"></a>[minimum value](#concept-meter-minimum)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;meter&#45;max"></a><strong><code>max</code></strong> getter steps are to return <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;this&#45;3"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;meter&#45;maximum"></a>[maximum value](#concept-meter-maximum)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;meter&#45;low"></a><strong><code>low</code></strong> getter steps are to return <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;this&#45;4"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;meter&#45;low"></a>[low boundary](#concept-meter-low)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;meter&#45;high"></a><strong><code>high</code></strong> getter steps are to return <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;this&#45;5"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;meter&#45;high"></a>[high boundary](#concept-meter-high)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;meter&#45;optimum"></a><strong><code>optimum</code></strong> getter steps are to return <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;this&#45;6"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;meter&#45;optimum"></a>[optimum value](#concept-meter-optimum)&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;lfe&#45;labels&#45;2"></a><code>[labels](#dom-lfe-labels)</code> IDL attribute provides a list of the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;meter&#45;element&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element"></a><code>[label](#the-label-element)</code>s&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following example shows how a gauge could fall back to localized or pretty&#45;printed text&#46;

``` text
<p>Disk usage: <meter min=0 value=170261928 max=233257824>170 261 928 bytes used
out of 233 257 824 bytes available</meter></p>
```

``` text
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFieldSetElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection elements;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);
};
```

The <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;represents"></a>[represents](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#represents) a set of form controls &#40;or other content&#41; grouped together&#44; optionally with a caption&#46; The caption is given by the first <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element that is a child of the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#44; if any&#46; The remainder of the descendants form the group&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;fieldset&#45;disabled"></a><strong><code>disabled</code></strong> attribute&#44; when specified&#44; causes all the form control descendants of the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#44; excluding those that are descendants of the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#39;s first <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element child&#44; if any&#44; to be <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;disabled"></a>[disabled](#concept-fe-disabled)&#46;

A <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element is a <a id="concept&#45;fieldset&#45;disabled"></a><strong>disabled fieldset</strong> if it matches any of the following conditions&#58;

- Its <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fieldset&#45;disabled&#45;2"></a><code>[disabled](#attr-fieldset-disabled)</code> attribute is specified&#46;
- It is a descendant of another <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element whose <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fieldset&#45;disabled&#45;3"></a><code>[disabled](#attr-fieldset-disabled)</code> attribute is specified&#44; and it is <em>not</em> a descendant of that <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#39;s first <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element child&#44; if any&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> attribute is used to explicitly associate the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element with its <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;form&#45;owner"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#46; The <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name&#45;2"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-name)</code> attribute represents the element&#39;s name&#46;

<strong><code><var>fieldset</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;fieldset&#45;type&#45;dev"></a>[type](#dom-fieldset-type)</code></strong>

Returns the string &#34;fieldset&#34;&#46;

<strong><code><var>fieldset</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;fieldset&#45;elements&#45;dev"></a>[elements](#dom-fieldset-elements)</code></strong>

Returns an <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;htmlcollection&#45;2"></a><code>[HTMLCollection](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection)</code> of the form controls in the element&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;fieldset&#45;type"></a><strong><code>type</code></strong> IDL attribute must return the string &#34;<code>fieldset</code>&#34;&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;fieldset&#45;elements"></a><strong><code>elements</code></strong> IDL attribute must return an <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;htmlcollection&#45;3"></a><code>[HTMLCollection](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection)</code> rooted at the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#44; whose filter matches <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;2"></a>[listed elements](#category-listed)&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;cva&#45;willvalidate&#45;2"></a><code>[willValidate](#dom-cva-willvalidate)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;cva&#45;validity&#45;2"></a><code>[validity](#dom-cva-validity)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;cva&#45;validationmessage&#45;2"></a><code>[validationMessage](#dom-cva-validationmessage)</code> attributes&#44; and the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;cva&#45;checkvalidity&#45;2"></a><code>[checkValidity&#40;&#41;](#dom-cva-checkvalidity)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;cva&#45;reportvalidity&#45;2"></a><code>[reportValidity&#40;&#41;](#dom-cva-reportvalidity)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;cva&#45;setcustomvalidity&#45;2"></a><code>[setCustomValidity&#40;&#41;](#dom-cva-setcustomvalidity)</code> methods&#44; are part of the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;constraint&#45;validation&#45;api"></a>[constraint validation API](#the-constraint-validation-api)&#46; The <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#dom-fae-form)</code> and <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;fieldset&#45;name"></a><code>[name](#dom-fieldset-name)</code> IDL attributes are part of the element&#39;s forms API&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This example shows a <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;10"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element being used to group a set of related controls&#58;

``` text
<fieldset>
 <legend>Display</legend>
 <p><label><input type=radio name=c value=0 checked> Black on White</label>
 <p><label><input type=radio name=c value=1> White on Black</label>
 <p><label><input type=checkbox name=g> Use grayscale</label>
 <p><label>Enhance contrast <input type=range name=e list=contrast min=0 max=100 value=0 step=1></label>
 <datalist id=contrast>
  <option label=Normal value=0>
  <option label=Maximum value=100>
 </datalist>
</fieldset>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following snippet shows a fieldset with a checkbox in the legend that controls whether or not the fieldset is enabled&#46; The contents of the fieldset consist of two required text controls and an optional year&#47;month control&#46;

``` text
<fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
 <legend> <label>
  <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
  Use Club Card
 </label> </legend>
 <p><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></p>
 <p><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></p>
 <p><label>Expiry date: <input name=clubexp type=month></label></p>
</fieldset>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

You can also nest <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;11"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> elements&#46; Here is an example expanding on the previous one that does so&#58;

``` text
<fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
 <legend> <label>
  <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
  Use Club Card
 </label> </legend>
 <p><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></p>
 <fieldset name="numfields">
  <legend> <label>
   <input type=radio checked name=clubtype onchange="form.numfields.disabled = !checked">
   My card has numbers on it
  </label> </legend>
  <p><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset name="letfields" disabled>
  <legend> <label>
   <input type=radio name=clubtype onchange="form.letfields.disabled = !checked">
   My card has letters on it
  </label> </legend>
  <p><label>Card code: <input name=clublet required pattern="[A-Za-z]+"></label></p>
 </fieldset>
</fieldset>
```

In this example&#44; if the outer &#34;Use Club Card&#34; checkbox is not checked&#44; everything inside the outer <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;12"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>&#44; including the two radio buttons in the legends of the two nested <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;13"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>s&#44; will be disabled&#46; However&#44; if the checkbox is checked&#44; then the radio buttons will both be enabled and will let you select which of the two inner <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;14"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code>s is to be enabled&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This example shows a grouping of controls where the <a id="the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element both labels the grouping&#44; and the nested heading element surfaces the grouping in the document outline&#58;

``` text
<fieldset>
 <legend> <h2>
  How can we best reach you?
 </h2> </legend>
 <p> <label>
 <input type=radio checked name=contact_pref>
  Phone
 </label> </p>
 <p> <label>
  <input type=radio name=contact_pref>
  Text
 </label> </p>
 <p> <label>
  <input type=radio name=contact_pref>
  Email
 </label> </p>
</fieldset>
```

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;categories"></a>[Categories](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-categories)&#58;</strong>

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;contexts"></a>[Contexts in which this element can be used](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-contexts)&#58;</strong>

As the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;first&#45;child&#45;2"></a>[first child](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-first-child) of an <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;optgroup&#45;element"></a><code>[optgroup](#the-optgroup-element)</code> element&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;content&#45;model"></a>[Content model](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-content-model)&#58;</strong>

If the element is a child of an <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;optgroup&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[optgroup](#the-optgroup-element)</code> element&#58; <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;phrasing&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[Phrasing content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#phrasing-content-2)&#44; but there must be no <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;interactive&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[interactive content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#interactive-content-2) and no descendant with the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;tabindex"></a><code>[tabindex](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-tabindex)</code> attribute&#46;

Otherwise&#58; <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;phrasing&#45;content&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[Phrasing content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#phrasing-content-2)&#44; optionally intermixed with <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;heading&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[heading content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#heading-content-2)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;tag&#45;omission"></a>[Tag omission in text&#47;html](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-tag-omission)&#58;</strong>

Neither tag is omissible&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;attributes"></a>[Content attributes](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-attributes)&#58;</strong>

<a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;global&#45;attributes"></a>[Global attributes](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#global-attributes)

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;accessibility&#45;considerations"></a>[Accessibility considerations](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-accessibility-considerations)&#58;</strong>

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-legend)&#46;

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-legend)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;sanitization"></a>[Sanitization](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-sanitization)&#58;</strong>

<a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;sanitizer&#45;uncategorized"></a>[Uncategorized](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#sanitizer-uncategorized)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;dom"></a>[DOM interface](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-dom)&#58;</strong>

<a id="htmllegendelement"></a><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;htmlelement"></a><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;htmlconstructor"></a><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;htmlformelement"></a><a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;legend&#45;form"></a>

``` text
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLLegendElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;represents"></a>[represents](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#represents) a caption for the rest of the contents of the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element&#39;s parent <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#44; if any&#46; Otherwise&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> has a parent <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;optgroup&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[optgroup](#the-optgroup-element)</code> element&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> represents the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;optgroup&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[optgroup](#the-optgroup-element)</code>&#39;s label&#46;

<strong><code><var>legend</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;legend&#45;form&#45;dev"></a>[form](#dom-legend-form)</code></strong>

Returns the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#44; if any&#44; or null otherwise&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;legend&#45;form"></a><strong><code>form</code></strong> IDL attribute&#39;s behavior depends on whether the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> element is in a <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element or not&#46; If the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;legend&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[legend](#the-legend-element)</code> has a <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element as its parent&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;legend&#45;form&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#dom-legend-form)</code> IDL attribute must return the same value as the <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><code>[form](#dom-fae-form)</code> IDL attribute on that <a id="the&#45;legend&#45;element&#58;the&#45;fieldset&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[fieldset](#the-fieldset-element)</code> element&#46; Otherwise&#44; it must return null&#46;

#### <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element"></a>4&#46;10&#46;17 The <strong><code>selectedcontent</code></strong> element[](#the-selectedcontent-element)

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;categories"></a>[Categories](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-categories)&#58;</strong>

<a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;phrasing&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[Phrasing content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#phrasing-content-2)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;contexts"></a>[Contexts in which this element can be used](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-contexts)&#58;</strong>

As a descendant of a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code> element which is a child of a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;content&#45;model"></a>[Content model](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-content-model)&#58;</strong>

<a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;content&#45;nothing"></a>[Nothing](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-content-nothing)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;tag&#45;omission"></a>[Tag omission in text&#47;html](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-tag-omission)&#58;</strong>

Neither tag is omissible&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;attributes"></a>[Content attributes](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-attributes)&#58;</strong>

<a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;global&#45;attributes"></a>[Global attributes](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#global-attributes)

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;accessibility&#45;considerations"></a>[Accessibility considerations](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-accessibility-considerations)&#58;</strong>

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-selectedcontent)&#46;

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-selectedcontent)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;sanitization"></a>[Sanitization](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-sanitization)&#58;</strong>

<a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;sanitizer&#45;uncategorized"></a>[Uncategorized](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#sanitizer-uncategorized)&#46;

<strong><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;dom"></a>[DOM interface](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-dom)&#58;</strong>

<a id="htmlselectedcontentelement"></a><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;htmlelement"></a><a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;htmlconstructor"></a>

``` text
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSelectedContentElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element reflects the contents of a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#39;s currently selected <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element&#46; <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> elements can be used to declaratively show the selected <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element&#39;s contents within the <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#39;s first child <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[button](#the-button-element)</code> element&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;option&#45;label"></a><code>[label](#attr-option-label)</code> attribute can be used to render a visible label for the option&#44; but the <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element will not reflect the content of the <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;option&#45;label&#45;2"></a><code>[label](#attr-option-label)</code> attribute&#46;

Every <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element has a boolean <a id="selectedcontent&#45;disabled"></a><strong>disabled</strong>&#44; which is initially false&#46;

To <a id="update&#45;a&#45;select&#39;s&#45;descendant&#45;selectedcontent&#45;elements"></a><strong>update a <code>select</code>&#39;s descendant <code>selectedcontent</code> elements</strong> given a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element <var>select</var>&#58;

1.  If <var>select</var> has the <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;select&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-select-multiple)</code> attribute&#44; then return&#46;

2.  Let <var>descendantSelectedcontents</var> be a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;list"></a>[list](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list) of <var>select</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;descendant"></a>[descendants](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant)&#44; in <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;tree&#45;order"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order)&#44; that are <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> elements whose <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) is false&#46;

3.  For each <var>selectedcontent</var> of <var>descendantSelectedcontents</var>&#58; <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;update&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent"></a>[update a <code>selectedcontent</code>](#update-a-selectedcontent) given <var>select</var> and <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

To <a id="update&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent"></a><strong>update a <code>selectedcontent</code></strong> given a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element <var>select</var> and a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element <var>selectedcontent</var>&#58;

1.  If <var>selectedcontent</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled&#45;2"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) is true&#44; then return&#46;

2.  Let <var>option</var> be the first <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> in <var>select</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;select&#45;option&#45;list"></a>[list of options](#concept-select-option-list) whose <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;selectedness"></a>[selectedness](#concept-option-selectedness) is true&#44; if any such <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> exists&#59; otherwise null&#46;

3.  If <var>option</var> is null&#44; then <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;clear&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent"></a>[clear a <code>selectedcontent</code>](#clear-a-selectedcontent) given <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

4.  Otherwise&#44; <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;clone&#45;an&#45;option&#45;into&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent"></a>[clone an option into a <code>selectedcontent</code>](#clone-an-option-into-a-selectedcontent) given <var>option</var> and <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

To <a id="clone&#45;an&#45;option&#45;into&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent"></a><strong>clone an <code>option</code> into a <code>selectedcontent</code></strong>&#44; given an <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element <var>option</var> and a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element <var>selectedcontent</var>&#58;

1.  Let <var>documentFragment</var> be the result of <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;create&#45;a&#45;document&#45;fragment"></a>[creating a document fragment](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#create-a-document-fragment) given <var>option</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;node&#45;document"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#46;

2.  For each <var>child</var> of <var>option</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;tree&#45;child"></a>[children](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-child)&#58;

    1.  Let <var>childClone</var> be the result of running <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;clone"></a>[clone](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-clone) given <var>child</var> with <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;clone&#45;subtree"></a>[subtree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#clone-a-node-subtree) set to true&#46;

    2.  <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;append"></a>[Append](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-append) <var>childClone</var> to <var>documentFragment</var>&#46;

3.  <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;replace&#45;all"></a>[Replace all](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace-all) with <var>documentFragment</var> within <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

To <a id="clear&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent"></a><strong>clear a <code>selectedcontent</code></strong> given a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element <var>selectedcontent</var>&#58;

1.  <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;replace&#45;all&#45;2"></a>[Replace all](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-replace-all) with null within <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;html&#45;element&#45;insertion&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element insertion steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-insertion-steps)&#44; given <var>selectedcontent</var>&#44; are to <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;recalculate&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#39;s&#45;disabledness"></a>[recalculate a <code>selectedcontent</code> element&#39;s disabledness](#recalculate-a-selectedcontent-element's-disabledness) given <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;10"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;html&#45;element&#45;post&#45;connection&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element post&#45;connection steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-post-connection-steps)&#44; given <var>selectedcontent</var>&#44; are&#58;

1.  Let <var>select</var> be the result of <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;recalculate&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#39;s&#45;disabledness&#45;2"></a>[recalculate a <code>selectedcontent</code> element&#39;s disabledness](#recalculate-a-selectedcontent-element's-disabledness) given <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

2.  If <var>selectedcontent</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled&#45;3"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) is true&#44; <var>select</var> is null&#44; or <var>select</var> has the <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;select&#45;multiple&#45;2"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-select-multiple)</code> attribute&#44; then return&#46;

3.  <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;update&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent&#45;2"></a>[Update a <code>selectedcontent</code>](#update-a-selectedcontent) given <var>select</var> and <var>selectedcontent</var>&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;11"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;html&#45;element&#45;moving&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element moving steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-moving-steps)&#44; given <var>movedNode</var>&#44; <var>isSubtreeRoot</var>&#44; and <var>oldAncestor</var>&#44; are&#58;

1.  Let <var>select</var> be the result of <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;recalculate&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#39;s&#45;disabledness&#45;3"></a>[recalculate a <code>selectedcontent</code> element&#39;s disabledness](#recalculate-a-selectedcontent-element's-disabledness) given <var>movedNode</var>&#46;

2.  If <var>movedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled&#45;4"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) is true&#44; <var>select</var> is null&#44; or <var>select</var> has the <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;select&#45;multiple&#45;3"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-select-multiple)</code> attribute&#44; then return&#46;

3.  <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;queue&#45;a&#45;microtask"></a>[Queue a microtask](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-a-microtask) to <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;update&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent&#45;3"></a>[update a <code>selectedcontent</code>](#update-a-selectedcontent) given <var>select</var> and <var>movedNode</var>&#46;

To <a id="recalculate&#45;a&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#39;s&#45;disabledness"></a><strong>recalculate a <code>selectedcontent</code> element&#39;s disabledness</strong>&#44; given a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;12"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element <var>selectedcontent</var>&#44; run these steps&#46; They return a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element or null&#46;

1.  Let <var>nearestSelectAncestor</var> be null&#46;

2.  Set <var>selectedcontent</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled&#45;5"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) to false&#46;

3.  For each <var>ancestor</var> of <var>selectedcontent</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;ancestor"></a>[ancestors](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-ancestor)&#44; in reverse <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;tree&#45;order&#45;2"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order)&#58;

    1.  If <var>ancestor</var> is a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#58;

        1.  If <var>nearestSelectAncestor</var> is null&#44; then set <var>nearestSelectAncestor</var> to <var>ancestor</var> and <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;continue"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue)&#46;

        2.  Set <var>selectedcontent</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled&#45;6"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) to true and <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;break"></a>[break](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break)&#46;

    2.  If <var>ancestor</var> is an <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element or a <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#45;13"></a><code>[selectedcontent](#the-selectedcontent-element)</code> element&#44; then set <var>selectedcontent</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;selectedcontent&#45;disabled&#45;7"></a>[disabled](#selectedcontent-disabled) to true and <a id="the&#45;selectedcontent&#45;element&#58;break&#45;2"></a>[break](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break)&#46;

4.  Return <var>nearestSelectAncestor</var>&#46;

#### <a id="form&#45;control&#45;infrastructure"></a>4&#46;10&#46;18 Form control infrastructure[](#form-control-infrastructure)

##### <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value"></a>4&#46;10&#46;18&#46;1 A form control&#39;s value[](#a-form-control's-value)

Most form controls have a <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a><strong>value</strong> and a <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;checked"></a><strong>checkedness</strong>&#46; &#40;The latter is only used by <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements&#46;&#41; These are used to describe how the user interacts with the control&#46;

A control&#39;s <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) is its internal state&#46; As such&#44; it might not match the user&#39;s current input&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For instance&#44; if a user enters the word &#34;three&#34; into <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;number&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;number&#41;"></a>[a numeric field](#number-state-(type=number)) that expects digits&#44; the user&#39;s input would be the string &#34;three&#34; but the control&#39;s <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) would remain unchanged&#46; Or&#44; if a user enters the email address &#34;  awesome&#64;example&#46;com&#34; &#40;with leading whitespace&#41; into <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;email&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;email&#41;"></a>[an email field](#email-state-(type=email))&#44; the user&#39;s input would be the string &#34;  awesome&#64;example&#46;com&#34; but the browser&#39;s UI for email fields might translate that into a <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) of &#34;<code>awesome&#64;example&#46;com</code>&#34; &#40;without the leading whitespace&#41;&#46;

<a id="concept&#45;input&#45;value&#45;dirty&#45;flag"></a><a id="concept&#45;textarea&#45;dirty"></a><a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> and <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements have a <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;dirty"></a><strong>dirty value flag</strong>&#46; This is used to track the interaction between the <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;4"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) and default value&#46; If it is false&#44; <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;5"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) mirrors the default value&#46; If it is true&#44; the default value is ignored&#46;

Some form controls also have an <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;optional&#45;value"></a><strong>optional value</strong>&#46; This largely mirrors the <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;6"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) but doesn&#39;t normalize to an empty string&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This ought to be used sparingly&#44; you generally want <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;7"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#46;

<a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code>&#44; <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>&#44; and <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> elements have a <a id="user&#45;validity"></a><strong>user validity</strong> boolean&#46; It is initially set to false&#46;

To define the behavior of constraint validation in the face of the <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute&#44; <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements can also have separately defined <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;values"></a><strong>value<em>s</em></strong>&#46;

To define the behavior of the <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;maxlength"></a><code>[maxlength](#attr-fe-maxlength)</code> and <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;minlength"></a><code>[minlength](#attr-fe-minlength)</code> attributes&#44; as well as other APIs specific to the <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> element&#44; all form control with a <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;8"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) also have an algorithm for obtaining an <a id="concept&#45;textarea&#45;api&#45;value"></a><a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;api&#45;value"></a><strong>API value</strong>&#46; By default this algorithm is to simply return the control&#39;s <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;9"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#46;

The <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element does not have a <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;10"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#59; the <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;selectedness"></a>[selectedness](#concept-option-selectedness) of its <a id="a&#45;form&#45;control&#39;s&#45;value&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> elements is what is used instead&#46;

##### <a id="mutability"></a>4&#46;10&#46;18&#46;2 Mutability[](#mutability)

A form control can be designated as <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;mutable"></a><strong>mutable</strong>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This determines &#40;by means of definitions and requirements in this specification that rely on whether an element is so designated&#41; whether or not the user can modify the <a id="mutability&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) or <a id="mutability&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;checked"></a>[checkedness](#concept-fe-checked) of a form control&#44; or whether or not a control can be automatically prefilled&#46;

##### <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms"></a>4&#46;10&#46;18&#46;3 Association of controls and forms[](#association-of-controls-and-forms)

A <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) can have a relationship with a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#44; which is called the element&#39;s <a id="form&#45;owner"></a><strong>form owner</strong>&#46; If a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) is not associated with a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#44; its <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) is said to be null&#46;

A <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) has an associated <a id="parser&#45;inserted&#45;flag"></a><strong>parser inserted flag</strong>&#46;

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Element&#47;input&#35;form](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#form)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

[Attributes&#35;attr&#45;form](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes#attr-form)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari≤4&#43;Chrome1&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera≤12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer≤6&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android≤12&#46;1&#43;

A <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) is&#44; by default&#44; associated with its nearest ancestor <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element &#40;as described below&#41;&#44; but&#44; if it is <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed"></a>[listed](#category-listed)&#44; may have a <a id="attr&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><strong><code>form</code></strong> attribute specified to override this&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This feature allows authors to work around the lack of support for nested <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> elements&#46;

If a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;2"></a>[listed](#category-listed) <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;5"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) has a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> attribute specified&#44; then that attribute&#39;s value must be the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;concept&#45;id"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) of a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element in the element&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;tree"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The rules in this section are complicated by the fact that although conforming documents or <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;tree&#45;2"></a>[trees](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree) will never contain nested <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> elements&#44; it is quite possible &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; using a script that performs DOM manipulation&#41; to generate <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;tree&#45;3"></a>[trees](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree) that have such nested elements&#46; They are also complicated by rules in the HTML parser that&#44; for historical reasons&#44; can result in a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;6"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) being associated with a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element that is not its ancestor&#46;

When a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;7"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) is created&#44; its <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;2"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) must be initialized to null &#40;no owner&#41;&#46;

When a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;8"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) is to be <a id="concept&#45;form&#45;association"></a><strong>associated</strong> with a form&#44; its <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;3"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) must be set to that form&#46;

When a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;3"></a>[listed](#category-listed) <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;9"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element)&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;2"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> attribute is set&#44; changed&#44; or removed&#44; then the user agent must <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner"></a>[reset the form owner](#reset-the-form-owner) of that element&#46;

When a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;4"></a>[listed](#category-listed) <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;10"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) has a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;3"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> attribute and the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;2"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) of any of the elements in the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;tree&#45;4"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree) changes&#44; then the user agent must <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner&#45;2"></a>[reset the form owner](#reset-the-form-owner) of that <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;11"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element)&#46;

When a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;5"></a>[listed](#category-listed) <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;12"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) has a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;4"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> attribute and an element with an <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;3"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) is <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;insert&#45;an&#45;element&#45;into&#45;a&#45;document"></a>[inserted into](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#insert-an-element-into-a-document) or <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;remove&#45;an&#45;element&#45;from&#45;a&#45;document"></a>[removed from](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#remove-an-element-from-a-document) the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document)</code>&#44; or its <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;html&#45;element&#45;moving&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element moving steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-moving-steps) are run&#44; then the user agent must <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner&#45;3"></a>[reset the form owner](#reset-the-form-owner) of that <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;13"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The form owner is also reset by the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;html&#45;element&#45;insertion&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element insertion steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-insertion-steps)&#44; <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;html&#45;element&#45;removing&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element removing steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-removing-steps)&#44; and <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;html&#45;element&#45;moving&#45;steps&#45;2"></a>[HTML element moving steps](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-moving-steps)&#46;

To <a id="reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner"></a><strong>reset the form owner</strong> of a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;14"></a>[form&#45;associated element](#form-associated-element) <var>element</var>&#58;

1.  Unset <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;parser&#45;inserted&#45;flag"></a>[parser inserted flag](#parser-inserted-flag)&#46;

2.  If all of the following are true&#58;

    - <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;4"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) is not null&#59;

    - <var>element</var> is not <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;6"></a>[listed](#category-listed) or its <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;5"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> content attribute is not present&#59; and

    - <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;5"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) is its nearest <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element ancestor after the change to the ancestor chain&#44;

    then return&#46;

3.  Set <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;6"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) to null&#46;

4.  If <var>element</var> is <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;7"></a>[listed](#category-listed)&#44; has a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;6"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> content attribute&#44; and is <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;connected"></a>[connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected)&#58;

    1.  If the first element in <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;tree&#45;5"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#44; in <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;tree&#45;order"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order)&#44; to have an <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;concept&#45;id&#45;4"></a>[ID](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-id) that is <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;identical&#45;to"></a>[identical to](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is) <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;7"></a><code>[form](#attr-fae-form)</code> content attribute&#39;s value&#44; is a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#44; then <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;concept&#45;form&#45;association"></a>[associate](#concept-form-association) the <var>element</var> with that <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;10"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#46;

5.  Otherwise&#44; if <var>element</var> has an ancestor <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;11"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#44; then <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;concept&#45;form&#45;association&#45;2"></a>[associate](#concept-form-association) <var>element</var> with the nearest such ancestor <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;12"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> element&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following non&#45;conforming snippet

``` text
...
 <form id="a">
  <div id="b"></div>
 </form>
 <script>
  document.getElementById('b').innerHTML =
     '<table><tr><td></form><form id="c"><input id="d"></table>' +
     '<input id="e">';
 </script>
...
```

the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;7"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) of &#34;d&#34; would be the inner nested form &#34;c&#34;&#44; while the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;8"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) of &#34;e&#34; would be the outer form &#34;a&#34;&#46;

This happens as follows&#58; First&#44; the &#34;e&#34; node gets associated with &#34;c&#34; in the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;html&#45;parser"></a>[HTML parser](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#html-parser)&#46; Then&#44; the <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;dom&#45;element&#45;innerhtml"></a><code>[innerHTML](html-language-dom-parsing--877d6146487f--c076ab7a56b9.md#dom-element-innerhtml)</code> algorithm moves the nodes from the temporary document to the &#34;b&#34; element&#46; At this point&#44; the nodes see their ancestor chain change&#44; and thus all the &#34;magic&#34; associations done by the parser are reset to normal ancestor associations&#46;

This example is a non&#45;conforming document&#44; though&#44; as it is a violation of the content models to nest <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;13"></a><code>[form](#the-form-element)</code> elements&#44; and there is a <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;parse&#45;errors"></a>[parse error](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#parse-errors) for the <code>&#60;&#47;form&#62;</code> tag&#46;

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;dev"></a>[form](#dom-fae-form)</code></strong>

<a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;category&#45;listed&#45;8"></a>[Listed](#category-listed) <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;15"></a>[form&#45;associated elements](#form-associated-element) except for <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#form-associated-custom-element) have a <a id="dom&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><strong><code>form</code></strong> IDL attribute&#44; which&#44; on getting&#44; must return the element&#39;s <a id="association&#45;of&#45;controls&#45;and&#45;forms&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;10"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#44; or null if there isn&#39;t one&#46;
