For the purposes of autofill&#44; a <a id="control&#39;s&#45;data"></a><strong>control&#39;s data</strong> depends on the kind of control&#58;

<strong>An <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element with its <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-input-type)</code> attribute in the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;email&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;email&#41;"></a>[Email](#email-state-(type=email)) state and with the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-input-multiple)</code> attribute specified</strong>

The element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;values"></a>[value<em>s</em>](#concept-fe-values)&#46;

<strong>Any other <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element</strong>

<strong>A <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> element</strong>

The element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#46;

<strong>A <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element with its <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;select&#45;multiple"></a><code>[multiple](#attr-select-multiple)</code> attribute specified</strong>

The <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> elements in the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;select&#45;option&#45;list"></a>[list of options](#concept-select-option-list) that have their <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;selectedness"></a>[selectedness](#concept-option-selectedness) set to true&#46;

<strong>Any other <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element</strong>

The <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> element in the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;select&#45;option&#45;list&#45;2"></a>[list of options](#concept-select-option-list) that has its <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;option&#45;selectedness&#45;2"></a>[selectedness](#concept-option-selectedness) set to true&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

How to process the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;hint&#45;set&#45;7"></a>[autofill hint set](#autofill-hint-set)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;scope&#45;4"></a>[autofill scope](#autofill-scope)&#44; and <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;8"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) depends on the mantle that the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;5"></a><code>[autocomplete](#attr-fe-autocomplete)</code> attribute is wearing&#46;

<strong>When wearing the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;expectation&#45;mantle"></a>[autofill expectation mantle](#autofill-expectation-mantle)&#46;&#46;&#46;</strong>

When an element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;9"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;off&#45;3"></a><code>[off](#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)</code>&#34;&#44; the user agent should not remember the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;control&#39;s&#45;data"></a>[control&#39;s data](#control's-data)&#44; and should not offer past values to the user&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In addition&#44; when an element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;10"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;off&#45;4"></a><code>[off](#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)</code>&#34;&#44; [values are reset](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#history-autocomplete) when <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;reactivate&#45;a&#45;document"></a>[reactivating a document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#reactivate-a-document)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Banks frequently do not want UAs to prefill login information&#58;

``` text
<p><label>Account: <input type="text" name="ac" autocomplete="off"></label></p>
<p><label>PIN: <input type="password" name="pin" autocomplete="off"></label></p>
```

When an element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;11"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is <em>not</em> &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;off&#45;5"></a><code>[off](#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)</code>&#34;&#44; the user agent may store the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;control&#39;s&#45;data&#45;2"></a>[control&#39;s data](#control's-data)&#44; and may offer previously stored values to the user&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; suppose a user visits a page with this control&#58;

``` text
<select name="country">
 <option>Afghanistan
 <option>Albania
 <option>Algeria
 <option>Andorra
 <option>Angola
 <option>Antigua and Barbuda
 <option>Argentina
 <option>Armenia
 <!-- ... -->
 <option>Yemen
 <option>Zambia
 <option>Zimbabwe
</select>
```

This might render as follows&#58;

![A drop&#45;down control with a long alphabetical list of countries&#46;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/select-country-1.png)

Suppose that on the first visit to this page&#44; the user selects &#34;Zambia&#34;&#46; On the second visit&#44; the user agent could duplicate the entry for Zambia at the top of the list&#44; so that the interface instead looks like this&#58;

![The same drop&#45;down control with the alphabetical list of countries&#44; but with Zambia as an entry at the top&#46;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/select-country-2.png)

When the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;12"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;on&#45;3"></a><code>[on](#attr-fe-autocomplete-on)</code>&#34;&#44; the user agent should attempt to use heuristics to determine the most appropriate values to offer the user&#44; e&#46;g&#46; based on the element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name"></a><code>[name](#attr-fe-name)</code> value&#44; the position of the element in its <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;tree"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#44; what other fields exist in the form&#44; and so forth&#46;

When the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;13"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is one of the names of the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;2"></a>[autofill fields](#autofill-field) described above&#44; the user agent should provide suggestions that match the meaning of the field name as given in the table earlier in this section&#46; The <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;hint&#45;set&#45;8"></a>[autofill hint set](#autofill-hint-set) should be used to select amongst multiple possible suggestions&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; if a user once entered one address into fields that used the &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;shipping&#45;3"></a><code>[shipping](#attr-fe-autocomplete-shipping)</code>&#34; keyword&#44; and another address into fields that used the &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;billing&#45;3"></a><code>[billing](#attr-fe-autocomplete-billing)</code>&#34; keyword&#44; then in subsequent forms only the first address would be suggested for form controls whose <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;hint&#45;set&#45;9"></a>[autofill hint set](#autofill-hint-set) contains the keyword &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;shipping&#45;4"></a><code>[shipping](#attr-fe-autocomplete-shipping)</code>&#34;&#46; Both addresses might be suggested&#44; however&#44; for address&#45;related form controls whose <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;hint&#45;set&#45;10"></a>[autofill hint set](#autofill-hint-set) does not contain either keyword&#46;

<strong>When wearing the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;anchor&#45;mantle&#45;3"></a>[autofill anchor mantle](#autofill-anchor-mantle)&#46;&#46;&#46;</strong>

When the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;14"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is not the empty string&#44; then the user agent must act as if the user had specified the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;control&#39;s&#45;data&#45;3"></a>[control&#39;s data](#control's-data) for the given <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;hint&#45;set&#45;11"></a>[autofill hint set](#autofill-hint-set)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;scope&#45;5"></a>[autofill scope](#autofill-scope)&#44; and <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;15"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) combination&#46;

When the user agent <a id="concept&#45;fe&#45;autofill"></a><strong>autofills form controls</strong>&#44; elements with the same <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;2"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) and the same <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;scope&#45;6"></a>[autofill scope](#autofill-scope) must use data relating to the same person&#44; address&#44; payment instrument&#44; and contact details&#46; <a id="autofill&#45;country"></a>When a user agent autofills &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;country&#45;2"></a><code>[country](#attr-fe-autocomplete-country)</code>&#34; and &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;country&#45;name&#45;2"></a><code>[country&#45;name](#attr-fe-autocomplete-country-name)</code>&#34; fields with the same <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;3"></a>[form owner](#form-owner) and <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;scope&#45;7"></a>[autofill scope](#autofill-scope)&#44; and the user agent has a value for the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;country&#45;3"></a><code>[country](#attr-fe-autocomplete-country)</code>&#34; field&#40;s&#41;&#44; then the &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;country&#45;name&#45;3"></a><code>[country&#45;name](#attr-fe-autocomplete-country-name)</code>&#34; field&#40;s&#41; must be filled using a human&#45;readable name for the same country&#46; When a user agent fills in multiple fields at once&#44; all fields with the same <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;16"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;4"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#44; and <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;scope&#45;8"></a>[autofill scope](#autofill-scope) must be filled with the same value&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Suppose a user agent knows of two phone numbers&#44; &#43;1 555 123 1234 and &#43;1 555 666 7777&#46; It would not be conforming for the user agent to fill a field with <code>autocomplete&#61;&#34;shipping tel&#45;local&#45;prefix&#34;</code> with the value &#34;123&#34; and another field in the same form with <code>autocomplete&#61;&#34;shipping tel&#45;local&#45;suffix&#34;</code> with the value &#34;7777&#34;&#46; The only valid prefilled values given the aforementioned information would be &#34;123&#34; and &#34;1234&#34;&#44; or &#34;666&#34; and &#34;7777&#34;&#44; respectively&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Similarly&#44; if a form for some reason contained both a &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;cc&#45;exp&#45;3"></a><code>[cc&#45;exp](#attr-fe-autocomplete-cc-exp)</code>&#34; field and a &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;cc&#45;exp&#45;month&#45;2"></a><code>[cc&#45;exp&#45;month](#attr-fe-autocomplete-cc-exp-month)</code>&#34; field&#44; and the user agent prefilled the form&#44; then the month component of the former would have to match the latter&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This requirement interacts with the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;anchor&#45;mantle&#45;4"></a>[autofill anchor mantle](#autofill-anchor-mantle) also&#46; Consider the following markup snippet&#58;

``` text
<form>
 <input type=hidden autocomplete="nickname" value="TreePlate">
 <input type=text autocomplete="nickname">
</form>
```

The only value that a conforming user agent could suggest in the text control is &#34;TreePlate&#34;&#44; the value given by the hidden <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#46;

The &#34;<code>section&#45;&#42;</code>&#34; tokens in the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;scope&#45;9"></a>[autofill scope](#autofill-scope) are opaque&#59; user agents must not attempt to derive meaning from the precise values of these tokens&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; it would not be conforming if the user agent decided that it should offer the address it knows to be the user&#39;s daughter&#39;s address for &#34;<code>section&#45;child</code>&#34; and the addresses it knows to be the user&#39;s spouses&#39; addresses for &#34;<code>section&#45;spouse</code>&#34;&#46;

The autocompletion mechanism must be implemented by the user agent acting as if the user had modified the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;control&#39;s&#45;data&#45;4"></a>[control&#39;s data](#control's-data)&#44; and must be done at a time where the element is <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;mutable"></a>[mutable](#concept-fe-mutable) &#40;e&#46;g&#46; just after the element has been inserted into the document&#44; or when the user agent <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;stop&#45;parsing"></a>[stops parsing](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#stop-parsing)&#41;&#46; User agents must only prefill controls using values that the user could have entered&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; if a <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element only has <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;option&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[option](#the-option-element)</code> elements with values &#34;Steve&#34; and &#34;Rebecca&#34;&#44; &#34;Jay&#34;&#44; and &#34;Bob&#34;&#44; and has an <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;17"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;given&#45;name&#45;2"></a><code>[given&#45;name](#attr-fe-autocomplete-given-name)</code>&#34;&#44; but the user agent&#39;s only idea for what to prefill the field with is &#34;Evan&#34;&#44; then the user agent cannot prefill the field&#46; It would not be conforming to somehow set the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;select&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[select](#the-select-element)</code> element to the value &#34;Evan&#34;&#44; since the user could not have done so themselves&#46;

A user agent prefilling a form control must not discriminate between form controls that are <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;in&#45;a&#45;document&#45;tree"></a>[in a document tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree) and those that are <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;connected"></a>[connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected)&#59; that is&#44; it is not conforming to make the decision on whether or not to autofill based on whether the element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;root"></a>[root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root) is a <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;shadow&#45;root"></a>[shadow root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root) versus a <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document)</code>&#46;

A user agent prefilling a form control&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) must not cause that control to <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;a&#45;type&#45;mismatch"></a>[suffer from a type mismatch](#suffering-from-a-type-mismatch)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;being&#45;too&#45;long"></a>[suffer from being too long](#suffering-from-being-too-long)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;being&#45;too&#45;short"></a>[suffer from being too short](#suffering-from-being-too-short)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;underflow"></a>[suffer from an underflow](#suffering-from-an-underflow)&#44; <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;an&#45;overflow"></a>[suffer from an overflow](#suffering-from-an-overflow)&#44; or <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;a&#45;step&#45;mismatch"></a>[suffer from a step mismatch](#suffering-from-a-step-mismatch)&#46; A user agent prefilling a form control&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value) must not cause that control to <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;suffering&#45;from&#45;a&#45;pattern&#45;mismatch"></a>[suffer from a pattern mismatch](#suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch) either&#46; Where possible given the control&#39;s constraints&#44; user agents must use the format given as canonical in the aforementioned table&#46; Where it&#39;s not possible for the canonical format to be used&#44; user agents should use heuristics to attempt to convert values so that they can be used&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; if the user agent knows that the user&#39;s middle name is &#34;Ines&#34;&#44; and attempts to prefill a form control that looks like this&#58;

``` text
<input name=middle-initial maxlength=1 autocomplete="additional-name">
```

&#46;&#46;&#46;then the user agent could convert &#34;Ines&#34; to &#34;I&#34; and prefill it that way&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A more elaborate example would be with month values&#46; If the user agent knows that the user&#39;s birthday is the 27th of July 2012&#44; then it might try to prefill all of the following controls with slightly different values&#44; all driven from this information&#58;

<table><tr><td>       <code>&lt;input name&#61;b type&#61;month autocomplete&#61;&#34;bday&#34;&gt;</code>      </td><td>       2012&#45;07      </td><td>       The day is dropped since the <a href="#month-state-(type=month)" id="autofill-processing-model:month-state-(type=month)">Month</a> state only accepts a       month&#47;year combination&#46; &#40;Note that this example is non&#45;conforming&#44; because the <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="autofill-processing-model:autofill-field-name-18">autofill       field name</a> <code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-bday-2"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-bday">bday</a></code> is not allowed with the       <a href="#month-state-(type=month)" id="autofill-processing-model:month-state-(type=month)-2">Month</a> state&#46;&#41;     </td></tr><tr><td>       <code>&lt;select name&#61;c autocomplete&#61;&#34;bday&#34;&gt;&#10; &lt;option&gt;Jan&#10; &lt;option&gt;Feb&#10; &#46;&#46;&#46;&#10; &lt;option&gt;Jul&#10; &lt;option&gt;Aug&#10; &#46;&#46;&#46;&#10;&lt;&#47;select&gt;</code>      </td><td>       July      </td><td>       The user agent picks the month from the listed options&#44; either by noticing there are twelve       options and picking the 7th&#44; or by recognizing that one of the strings &#40;three characters &#34;Jul&#34;       followed by a newline and a space&#41; is a close match for the name of the month &#40;July&#41; in one of       the user agent&#39;s supported languages&#44; or through some other similar mechanism&#46;     </td></tr><tr><td>       <code>&lt;input name&#61;a type&#61;number min&#61;1 max&#61;12 autocomplete&#61;&#34;bday&#45;month&#34;&gt;</code>      </td><td>       7      </td><td>       User agent converts &#34;July&#34; to a month number in the range 1&#46;&#46;12&#44; like the field&#46;     </td></tr><tr><td>       <code>&lt;input name&#61;a type&#61;number min&#61;0 max&#61;11 autocomplete&#61;&#34;bday&#45;month&#34;&gt;</code>      </td><td>       6      </td><td>       User agent converts &#34;July&#34; to a month number in the range 0&#46;&#46;11&#44; like the field&#46;     </td></tr><tr><td>       <code>&lt;input name&#61;a type&#61;number min&#61;1 max&#61;11 autocomplete&#61;&#34;bday&#45;month&#34;&gt;</code>      </td><td>      </td><td>       User agent doesn&#39;t fill in the field&#44; since it can&#39;t make a good guess as to what the form expects&#46;    </td></tr></table>

A user agent may allow the user to override an element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;19"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name)&#44; e&#46;g&#46; to change it from &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;off&#45;6"></a><code>[off](#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)</code>&#34; to &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;on&#45;4"></a><code>[on](#attr-fe-autocomplete-on)</code>&#34; to allow values to be remembered and prefilled despite the page author&#39;s objections&#44; or to always &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;off&#45;7"></a><code>[off](#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)</code>&#34;&#44; never remembering values&#46;

More specifically&#44; user agents may in particular consider replacing the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;20"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) of form controls that match the description given in the first column of the following table&#44; when their <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;21"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) is either &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;on&#45;5"></a><code>[on](#attr-fe-autocomplete-on)</code>&#34; or &#34;<a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete&#45;off&#45;8"></a><code>[off](#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)</code>&#34;&#44; with the value given in the second cell of that row&#46; If this table is used&#44; the replacements must be done in <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;tree&#45;order"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order)&#44; since all but the first row references the <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;autofill&#45;field&#45;name&#45;22"></a>[autofill field name](#autofill-field-name) of earlier elements&#46; When the descriptions below refer to form controls being preceded or followed by others&#44; they mean in the list of <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;category&#45;listed"></a>[listed elements](#category-listed) that share the same <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;5"></a>[form owner](#form-owner)&#46;

<table><thead><tr><th>Form control      </th><th>New <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="autofill-processing-model:autofill-field-name-23">autofill field name</a>     </th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>        an <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-5"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-input-type-2"><a href="#attr-input-type">type</a></code> attribute is in       the <a href="#text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)" id="autofill-processing-model:text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)">Text</a> state that is followed by an       <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-6"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-input-type-3"><a href="#attr-input-type">type</a></code> attribute is in       the <a href="#password-state-(type=password)" id="autofill-processing-model:password-state-(type=password)">Password</a> state       </td><td>        &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-username-2"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-username">username</a></code>&#34;       </td></tr><tr><td>        an <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-7"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-input-type-4"><a href="#attr-input-type">type</a></code> attribute is in       the <a href="#password-state-(type=password)" id="autofill-processing-model:password-state-(type=password)-2">Password</a> state that is preceded by an       <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-8"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="autofill-processing-model:autofill-field-name-24">autofill field name</a> is &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-username-3"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-username">username</a></code>&#34;       </td><td>        &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-current-password-2"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-current-password">current&#45;password</a></code>&#34;       </td></tr><tr><td>        an <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-9"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-input-type-5"><a href="#attr-input-type">type</a></code> attribute is in       the <a href="#password-state-(type=password)" id="autofill-processing-model:password-state-(type=password)-3">Password</a> state that is preceded by an       <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-10"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="autofill-processing-model:autofill-field-name-25">autofill field name</a> is &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-current-password-3"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-current-password">current&#45;password</a></code>&#34;       </td><td>        &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-new-password-2"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-new-password">new&#45;password</a></code>&#34;       </td></tr><tr><td>        an <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-11"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-input-type-6"><a href="#attr-input-type">type</a></code> attribute is in       the <a href="#password-state-(type=password)" id="autofill-processing-model:password-state-(type=password)-4">Password</a> state that is preceded by an       <code id="autofill-processing-model:the-input-element-12"><a href="#the-input-element">input</a></code> element whose <a href="#autofill-field-name" id="autofill-processing-model:autofill-field-name-26">autofill field name</a> is &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-new-password-3"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-new-password">new&#45;password</a></code>&#34;       </td><td>        &#34;<code id="autofill-processing-model:attr-fe-autocomplete-new-password-4"><a href="#attr-fe-autocomplete-new-password">new&#45;password</a></code>&#34;     </td></tr></tbody></table>

The <a id="dom&#45;fe&#45;autocomplete"></a><strong><code>autocomplete</code></strong> IDL attribute&#44; on getting&#44; must return the element&#39;s <a id="autofill&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;idl&#45;exposed&#45;autofill&#45;value&#45;5"></a>[IDL&#45;exposed autofill value](#idl-exposed-autofill-value)&#46;

#### <a id="textFieldSelection"></a>4&#46;10&#46;20 APIs for the text control selections[](#textFieldSelection)

The <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> and <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements define several attributes and methods for handling their selection&#46; Their shared algorithms are defined here&#46;

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;select&#45;dev"></a>[select](#dom-textarea/input-select)&#40;&#41;</code></strong>

Selects everything in the text control&#46;

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectionstart&#45;dev"></a>[selectionStart](#dom-textarea/input-selectionstart) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns the offset to the start of the selection&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the start of the selection&#46;

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectionend&#45;dev"></a>[selectionEnd](#dom-textarea/input-selectionend) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns the offset to the end of the selection&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the end of the selection&#46;

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectiondirection&#45;dev"></a>[selectionDirection](#dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns the current direction of the selection&#46;

Can be set&#44; to change the direction of the selection&#46;

The possible values are &#34;<code>forward</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>backward</code>&#34;&#44; and &#34;<code>none</code>&#34;&#46;

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;setselectionrange&#45;dev"></a>[setSelectionRange](#dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange)&#40;<var>start</var>&#44; <var>end</var> &#91;&#44; <var>direction</var>&#93;&#41;</code></strong>

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android&#63;

Replaces a range of text with the new text&#46; If the <var>start</var> and <var>end</var> arguments are not provided&#44; the range is assumed to be the selection&#46;

The final argument determines how the selection will be set after the text has been replaced&#46; The possible values are&#58;

<strong>&#34;<a id="dom&#45;selectionmode&#45;select&#45;dev"></a><code>[select](#dom-selectionmode-select)</code>&#34;</strong>

Selects the newly inserted text&#46;

<strong>&#34;<a id="dom&#45;selectionmode&#45;start&#45;dev"></a><code>[start](#dom-selectionmode-start)</code>&#34;</strong>

Moves the selection to just before the inserted text&#46;

<strong>&#34;<a id="dom&#45;selectionmode&#45;end&#45;dev"></a><code>[end](#dom-selectionmode-end)</code>&#34;</strong>

Moves the selection to just after the selected text&#46;

<strong>&#34;<a id="dom&#45;selectionmode&#45;preserve&#45;dev"></a><code>[preserve](#dom-selectionmode-preserve)</code>&#34;</strong>

Attempts to preserve the selection&#46; This is the default&#46;

All <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements to which these APIs <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;input&#45;apply"></a>[apply](#concept-input-apply)&#44; and all <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements&#44; have either a <a id="concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection"></a><strong>selection</strong> or a <a id="concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor"></a><strong>text entry cursor position</strong> at all times &#40;even for elements that are not <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;being&#45;rendered"></a>[being rendered](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#being-rendered)&#41;&#44; measured in offsets into the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;code&#45;unit"></a>[code units](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit) of the control&#39;s <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#46; The initial state must consist of a <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor"></a>[text entry cursor](#concept-textarea/input-cursor) at the beginning of the control&#46;

For <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> elements&#44; these APIs must operate on the element&#39;s <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value"></a>[value](#concept-fe-value)&#46; For <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements&#44; these APIs must operate on the element&#39;s <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;api&#45;value"></a>[API value](#concept-fe-api-value)&#46; In the below algorithms&#44; we call the value string being operated on the <a id="concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value"></a><strong>relevant value</strong>&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The use of <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;api&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[API value](#concept-fe-api-value) instead of <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#45;raw&#45;value"></a>[raw value](#concept-textarea-raw-value) for <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements means that U&#43;000D &#40;CR&#41; characters are normalized away&#46; For example&#44;

``` text
<textarea id="demo"></textarea>
<script>
 demo.value = "A\r\nB";
 demo.setRangeText("replaced", 0, 2);
 assert(demo.value === "replacedB");
</script>
```

If we had operated on the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#45;raw&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[raw value](#concept-textarea-raw-value) of &#34;<code>A&#92;r&#92;nB</code>&#34;&#44; then we would have replaced the characters &#34;<code>A&#92;r</code>&#34;&#44; ending up with a result of &#34;<code>replaced&#92;nB</code>&#34;&#46; But since we used the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;api&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[API value](#concept-fe-api-value) of &#34;<code>A&#92;nB</code>&#34;&#44; we replaced the characters &#34;<code>A&#92;n</code>&#34;&#44; giving &#34;<code>replacedB</code>&#34;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Characters with no visible rendering&#44; such as U&#43;200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER&#44; still count as characters&#46; Thus&#44; for instance&#44; the selection can include just an invisible character&#44; and the text insertion cursor can be placed to one side or another of such a character&#46;

Whenever the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value) changes for an element to which these APIs apply&#44; run these steps&#58;

1.  If the element has a <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection"></a>[selection](#concept-textarea/input-selection)&#58;

    1.  If the start of the selection is now past the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#44; set it to the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;4"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#46;

    2.  If the end of the selection is now past the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;5"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#44; set it to the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;6"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#46;

    3.  If the user agent does not support empty selection&#44; and both the start and end of the selection are now pointing to the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;7"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#44; then instead set the element&#39;s <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor&#45;2"></a>[text entry cursor position](#concept-textarea/input-cursor) to the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;8"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#44; removing any selection&#46;

2.  Otherwise&#44; the element must have a <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor&#45;3"></a>[text entry cursor position](#concept-textarea/input-cursor) position&#46; If it is now past the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;9"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#44; set it to the end of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;10"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In some cases where the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;11"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value) changes&#44; other parts of the specification will also modify the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor&#45;4"></a>[text entry cursor position](#concept-textarea/input-cursor)&#44; beyond just the clamping steps above&#46; For example&#44; see the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;dom&#45;textarea&#45;value"></a><code>[value](#dom-textarea-value)</code> setter for <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code>&#46;

Where possible&#44; user interface features for changing the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection&#45;2"></a>[text selection](#concept-textarea/input-selection) in <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> and <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements must be implemented using the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;set&#45;the&#45;selection&#45;range"></a>[set the selection range](#set-the-selection-range) algorithm so that&#44; e&#46;g&#46;&#44; all the same events fire&#46;

The <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection&#45;3"></a>[selections](#concept-textarea/input-selection) of <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> and <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[textarea](#the-textarea-element)</code> elements have a <a id="selection&#45;direction"></a><strong>selection direction</strong>&#44; which is either &#34;<code>forward</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>backward</code>&#34;&#44; or &#34;<code>none</code>&#34;&#46; The exact meaning of the selection direction depends on the platform&#46; This direction is set when the user manipulates the selection&#46; The initial <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;selection&#45;direction"></a>[selection direction](#selection-direction) must be &#34;<code>none</code>&#34; if the platform supports that direction&#44; or &#34;<code>forward</code>&#34; otherwise&#46;

To <a id="set&#45;the&#45;selection&#45;direction"></a><strong>set the selection direction</strong> of an element to a given direction&#44; update the element&#39;s <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;selection&#45;direction&#45;2"></a>[selection direction](#selection-direction) to the given direction&#44; unless the direction is &#34;<code>none</code>&#34; and the platform does not support that direction&#59; in that case&#44; update the element&#39;s <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;selection&#45;direction&#45;3"></a>[selection direction](#selection-direction) to &#34;<code>forward</code>&#34;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

On Windows&#44; the direction indicates the position of the caret relative to the selection&#58; a &#34;<code>forward</code>&#34; selection has the caret at the end of the selection and a &#34;<code>backward</code>&#34; selection has the caret at the start of the selection&#46; Windows has no &#34;<code>none</code>&#34; direction&#46;

On Mac&#44; the direction indicates which end of the selection is affected when the user adjusts the size of the selection using the arrow keys with the Shift modifier&#58; the &#34;<code>forward</code>&#34; direction means the end of the selection is modified&#44; and the &#34;<code>backward</code>&#34; direction means the start of the selection is modified&#46; The &#34;<code>none</code>&#34; direction is the default on Mac&#44; it indicates that no particular direction has yet been selected&#46; The user sets the direction implicitly when first adjusting the selection&#44; based on which directional arrow key was used&#46;

1.  If this element is an <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; and either <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;select"></a><code>[select&#40;&#41;](#dom-textarea/input-select)</code> <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;do&#45;not&#45;apply"></a>[does not apply](#do-not-apply) to this element or the corresponding control has no selectable text&#44; return&#46;

If there is no <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection&#45;4"></a>[selection](#concept-textarea/input-selection)&#44; return the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;code&#45;unit&#45;2"></a>[code unit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit) offset within the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;12"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value) to the character that immediately follows the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor&#45;5"></a>[text entry cursor](#concept-textarea/input-cursor)&#46;

3.  Return the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;code&#45;unit&#45;3"></a>[code unit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit) offset within the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;13"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value) to the character that immediately follows the start of the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection&#45;5"></a>[selection](#concept-textarea/input-selection)&#46;

The <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectionstart&#45;2"></a><code>[selectionStart](#dom-textarea/input-selectionstart)</code> attribute&#39;s setter must run the following steps&#58;

The <a id="dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectionend"></a><strong><code>selectionEnd</code></strong> attribute&#39;s getter must run the following steps&#58;

1.  If this element is an <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[input](#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; and <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectionend&#45;2"></a><code>[selectionEnd](#dom-textarea/input-selectionend)</code> <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;do&#45;not&#45;apply&#45;4"></a>[does not apply](#do-not-apply) to this element&#44; return null&#46;

If there is no <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selection&#45;6"></a>[selection](#concept-textarea/input-selection)&#44; return the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;code&#45;unit&#45;4"></a>[code unit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit) offset within the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;relevant&#45;value&#45;14"></a>[relevant value](#concept-textarea/input-relevant-value) to the character that immediately follows the <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;concept&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;cursor&#45;6"></a>[text entry cursor](#concept-textarea/input-cursor)&#46;

The <a id="textFieldSelection&#58;dom&#45;textarea&#47;input&#45;selectionend&#45;3"></a><code>[selectionEnd](#dom-textarea/input-selectionend)</code> attribute&#39;s setter must run the following steps&#58;
